title.zh: 卷94 閹官:宗愛 仇洛齊 段霸 王琚 趙黑 孫小 張宗之等
title.en: Volume 94: Eunuchs - Zong Ai, Chou Luoqi, Duan Ba, Wang Ju, Zhao Hei, Sun Xiao, Zhang Zongzhi, and others
title.raw: 卷94 閹官:宗愛 仇洛齊 段霸 王琚 趙黑 孫小 張宗之等 Volume 94: Eunuchs - Zong Ai, Chou Luoqi, Duan Ba, Wang Ju, Zhao Hei, Sun Xiao, Zhang Zongzhi, and others

sentences.zh: 宗愛 仇洛齊 段霸 王琚 趙黑[1] 孫小 張宗之 劇鵬 張祐 抱嶷 王遇 苻承祖 王質 李堅 秦松 白整 劉騰 賈粲 楊範 成軌 王溫 孟鸞[2] 平季 封津 劉思逸

translations.literal: Zong Ai, Chou Luoqi, Duan Ba, Wang Ju, Zhao Hei, Sun Xiao, Zhang Zongzhi, Ju Peng, Zhang You, Bao Ni, Wang Yu, Fu Chengzu, Wang Zhi, Li Jian, Qin Song, Bai Zheng, Liu Teng, Jia Can, Yang Fan, Cheng Gui, Wang Wen, Meng Luan, Ping Ji, Feng Jin, Liu Siyi.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ai, Chou Luoqi, Duan Ba, Wang Ju, Zhao Hei, Sun Xiao, Zhang Zongzhi, Ju Peng, Zhang You, Bao Ni, Wang Yu, Fu Chengzu, Wang Zhi, Li Jian, Qin Song, Bai Zheng, Liu Teng, Jia Can, Yang Fan, Cheng Gui, Wang Wen, Meng Luan, Ping Ji, Feng Jin, and Liu Siyi.

sentences.zh: 夫宮腐之族，置於閽寺，取則天象，事歷百王。

translations.literal: As for the class of palace-castrated men, placed in gate-palace offices, they follow the pattern of heaven's signs; the institution has endured through a hundred kings.
translations.idiomatic: The palace eunuch caste was installed at the gate-palaces in imitation of celestial portents, and rulers of a hundred generations have maintained the office.

sentences.zh: 身乖全品，任事宮掖，親由褻狎，恩生趨走，便僻俯仰，當寵擅權。

translations.literal: Their bodies fall short of full human status; they serve in the inner palace; intimacy arises from familiar dalliance, favor from running to and fro; through flattery and bowing they come to wield power when favored.
translations.idiomatic: Denied full humanity, they served in the women's quarters; closeness bred through intimate familiarity, favor through constant attendance; with obsequious gestures they rose to dominate whenever they won the ruler's trust.

sentences.zh: 斯則伊戾、豎刁因而禍兩國，石顯、張讓所以翦二京也。

translations.literal: Thus Yi Li and Shu Diao brought disaster to two states; Shi Xian and Zhang Rang were how the two capitals were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: This was how Yi Li and Shu Diao ruined two kingdoms, and how Shi Xian and Zhang Rang brought down the two imperial capitals.

sentences.zh: 豈非形質既虧，生命易忽，譬之胥靡，不懼登高。

translations.literal: Is it not that once their physical form is impaired, life is easily held cheap—like convict laborers, they do not fear climbing high?
translations.idiomatic: Once their bodies were marred, life counted for little; like felons under sentence, they had no fear of heights.

sentences.zh: 此亦苟且之事，由變不已也。

translations.literal: This too is a matter of making do as circumstances shift, change upon change without end.
translations.idiomatic: Such conduct was merely opportunism, shifting endlessly with each new turn of events.

sentences.zh: 王者殷鑒，宜改往轍，而後庭婉孌遊宴之地，椒壼留連，終見任使。

translations.literal: Kings should take past examples as mirrors and change the old course, yet in the rear courtyard where lovely ones feast and roam, lingering in the pepper chambers, they are still employed in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers ought to learn from past examples and mend their ways, yet in the rear palace where beauties feast and linger in the women's quarters, eunuchs are still entrusted with office in the end.

sentences.zh: 巧佞由之而自達，權幸俄然而復歸。

translations.literal: Through them the crafty and fawning advance themselves; power and favor swiftly return.
translations.idiomatic: Crafty flatterers gained access through them, and influence and favor soon flowed back to them once more.

sentences.zh: 斯蓋其由來遠矣，非一朝一世也。

translations.literal: The roots of this run far back; it is not a matter of a single dynasty or age.
translations.idiomatic: The practice had deep roots; it was not confined to one reign or one era.

sentences.zh: 魏氏則宗愛殺帝害王，劉騰廢后戮相，其間竊官爵，盜財賄，乘勢使氣為朝野之患者，何可勝舉。

translations.literal: Under the Wei, Zong Ai killed emperors and harmed princes; Liu Teng deposed the empress and slaughtered a chancellor; between them, those who stole offices and ranks, plundered bribes, and rode their power to bully court and countryside as a scourge—how could they be counted?
translations.idiomatic: Under the Northern Wei, Zong Ai murdered emperors and princes, and Liu Teng deposed an empress and killed a chief minister; besides them, countless others stole offices, seized bribes, and abused their position to tyrannize court and realm.

sentences.zh: 今謹錄其尤顯焉。

translations.literal: Here we record only the most conspicuous cases.
translations.idiomatic: Below we record only the most notorious among them.

sentences.zh: 恭宗之監國也，每事精察。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong oversaw the state as crown prince, he examined every matter with keen scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: While Crown Prince Gong was supervising the realm, he scrutinized every affair with exacting care.

sentences.zh: 愛天性險暴，行多非法，恭宗每銜之。

translations.literal: Ai was by nature cruel and violent, his conduct often unlawful; Gong harbored resentment toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Ai was cruel and violent by nature and often acted outside the law; the crown prince bore a deep grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 給事仇尼道盛、侍郎任平城等任事東宮，微為權勢，世祖頗聞之。

translations.literal: The attendant Chou Ni Daosheng, the vice director Ren Pingcheng, and others serving in the Eastern Palace wielded a measure of power; Emperor Shizu heard of it.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant Chou Ni Daosheng, Vice Director Ren Pingcheng, and others who served in the crown prince's household had begun to wield some influence, and Emperor Taiwu took notice.

sentences.zh: 二人與愛並不睦。

translations.literal: The two men were not on good terms with Ai.
translations.idiomatic: The two men were on bad terms with Ai.

sentences.zh: 為懼道盛等案其事，遂構告其罪。

translations.literal: Fearing that Daosheng and the others would investigate his affairs, he fabricated charges against them.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid that Daosheng and the others would investigate him, he fabricated charges and denounced them.

sentences.zh: 詔斬道盛等於都街。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Daosheng and the others beheaded in the capital street.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Daosheng and the others executed in the streets of the capital.

sentences.zh: 時世祖震怒，恭宗遂以憂薨。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Shizu was furious with rage, and Gong thereupon died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu was furious, and the crown prince died soon afterward, overcome by grief.

sentences.zh: 是後，世祖追悼恭宗，愛懼誅，遂謀逆。

translations.literal: Afterward, as Emperor Shizu mourned Gong, Ai feared execution and plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, as Emperor Taiwu mourned the crown prince, Ai feared he would be put to death and plotted treason.

sentences.zh: 二年春，世祖暴崩，愛所為也。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year, Emperor Shizu died suddenly; it was Ai's doing.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year, Emperor Taiwu died suddenly—it was Ai's work.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射蘭延、侍中吳興公和疋、侍中太原公薛提等祕不發喪。

translations.literal: Lan Yan, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, He Pi, Duke of Wuxing and Palace Attendant, Xue Ti, Duke of Taiyuan and Palace Attendant, and others kept the death secret and did not announce the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Yan, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, He Pi, Duke of Wuxing and Palace Attendant, Xue Ti, Duke of Taiyuan and Palace Attendant, and others concealed the emperor's death and did not announce the mourning.

sentences.zh: 延、疋二人議以高宗沖幼，欲立長子，徵秦王翰置之祕室。

translations.literal: Yan and Pi discussed that because Emperor Gaozong was young, they wished to install the eldest son, summoned Prince Qin Han, and placed him in a secret chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Pi argued that because the designated heir was still a child, they should enthrone the eldest son instead; they summoned Prince Qin Han and kept him in a hidden chamber.

sentences.zh: 提以高宗有世嫡之重，不可廢所宜立而更求君。

translations.literal: Ti held that Gaozong bore the weight of legitimate succession and that one could not set aside the rightful heir to seek another ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Ti argued that the designated heir held the status of legitimate succession and that they could not discard the rightful choice to seek another ruler.

sentences.zh: 延等猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Yan and the others hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and the others wavered, unable to reach a decision.

sentences.zh: 愛知其謀。

translations.literal: Ai learned of their plot.
translations.idiomatic: Ai learned of their plan.

sentences.zh: 始愛負罪於東宮，而與吳王余素協，乃密迎余自中宮便門入，矯皇后令徵延等。

translations.literal: At first Ai had been guilty toward the Eastern Palace, but he had long been in league with Prince Wu Yu; he secretly welcomed Yu through the inner palace side gate and forged an empress's order summoning Yan and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Ai had earlier incurred guilt toward the crown prince's household, but he had long been allied with Prince Wu Yu; he secretly brought Yu in through the inner palace side gate and forged an empress's order summoning Yan and the others.

sentences.zh: 延等以愛素賤，弗之疑，皆隨之入。

translations.literal: Yan and the others, because Ai had always been base-born, did not suspect him and all followed him inside.
translations.idiomatic: Because Ai had always been a man of low birth, Yan and the others suspected nothing and followed him inside.

sentences.zh: 愛先使閹豎三十人持仗於宮內，及延等入，以次收縛，斬於殿堂。

translations.literal: Ai had first stationed thirty eunuchs bearing weapons inside the palace; when Yan and the others entered, they were seized and bound in turn and beheaded in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Ai had already posted thirty armed eunuchs inside the palace; when Yan and the others entered, they were seized one by one and beheaded in the hall.

sentences.zh: 執秦王翰，殺之於永巷而立余。

translations.literal: They seized Prince Qin Han, killed him in the Long Lane, and installed Yu.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Prince Qin Han, killed him in the Long Lane, and enthroned Yu.

sentences.zh: 余以愛為大司馬、大將軍、太師、都督中外諸軍事，領中祕書，封馮翊王。

translations.literal: Yu appointed Ai Grand Marshal, Grand General, Grand Preceptor, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies at Home and Abroad, head of the Central Secretariat, and enfeoffed him as King of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu made Ai Grand Marshal, Grand General, Grand Preceptor, and supreme commander of all armies at home and abroad, put him in charge of the Central Secretariat, and enfeoffed him as King of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 愛既立余，位居元輔，錄三省，兼總戎禁，坐召公卿，權恣日甚，內外憚之。

translations.literal: Once Ai had installed Yu, he stood as chief minister, controlled the three secretariats, and also held overall command of the military guard; he summoned dukes and ministers to sit before him, his power grew more unrestrained day by day, and court and countryside feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Ai had put Yu on the throne, he became chief minister, controlled all three secretariats, and held command of the palace guard; he summoned nobles and ministers to attend him at will, his power grew daily, and the whole court feared him.

sentences.zh: 羣情咸以為愛必有趙高、閻樂之禍，余疑之，遂謀奪其權。

translations.literal: Public sentiment held that Ai would bring the calamity of a Zhao Gao or Yan Le; Yu grew suspicious and plotted to strip him of power.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone believed Ai would bring disaster like Zhao Gao or Yan Le; Yu grew suspicious and plotted to take his power away.

sentences.zh: 愛憤怒，使小黃門賈周等夜殺余，事在余傳。

translations.literal: Ai, enraged, had the junior palace attendant Jia Zhou and others kill Yu by night; the affair is recorded in Yu's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Ai had the junior palace attendant Jia Zhou and others assassinate Yu by night; the full account appears in Yu's biography.

sentences.zh: 高宗立，誅愛、周等，皆具五刑，夷三族。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, he executed Ai, Zhou, and the others, all suffering the five punishments in full, and exterminated their three clans.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wencheng ascended the throne, he executed Ai, Zhou, and the others with the full five punishments and exterminated their clans to the third degree.

sentences.zh: 仇洛齊，中山人，本姓侯氏。

translations.literal: Chou Luoqi was a man of Zhongshan; his original surname was Hou.
translations.idiomatic: Chou Luoqi was from Zhongshan; his original family name was Hou.

sentences.zh: 外祖父仇款，始出馮翊重泉。

translations.literal: His maternal grandfather Chou Kuan first came from Chongquan in Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal grandfather Chou Kuan's family originally came from Chongquan in Fengyi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 款，石虎末徙鄴南枋頭，仕慕容暐為烏丸護軍、長水校尉。

translations.literal: Kuan, at the end of Shi Hu's reign, moved to Fangtou south of Ye; he served Murong Wei as Wuhuan Protector-General and Colonel of the Long River.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Shi Hu's reign, Kuan moved to Fangtou south of Ye and served Murong Wei as Wuhuan Protector-General and Colonel of the Long River.

sentences.zh: 生二子，長曰嵩，小曰騰。

translations.literal: He had two sons: the elder was called Song, the younger Teng.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: the elder was Song, the younger Teng.

sentences.zh: 嵩仕慕容垂，遷居中山，位殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Song served Murong Chui, moved his residence to Zhongshan, and held the post of Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Song served Murong Chui, settled in Zhongshan, and rose to the post of Palace Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 嵩有二子，長曰廣，小曰盆。

translations.literal: Song had two sons: the elder was called Guang, the younger Pen.
translations.idiomatic: Song had two sons: the elder was Guang, the younger Pen.

sentences.zh: 洛齊生而非男，嵩養為子，因為之姓仇。

translations.literal: Luoqi was born not a male; Song adopted him as a son and therefore gave him the surname Chou.
translations.idiomatic: Luoqi was born a eunuch; Song adopted him as a son and gave him the surname Chou.

sentences.zh: 初嵩長女有姿色，充冉閔宮闈，閔破，入慕容儁，又轉賜盧豚。

translations.literal: At first Song's eldest daughter was beautiful and entered Ran Min's inner palace; when Min was defeated, she passed to Murong Jun, and was later transferred as a gift to Lu Tun.
translations.idiomatic: Song's eldest daughter was beautiful and entered Ran Min's harem; after Min's defeat she passed to Murong Jun, and was later given to Lu Tun.

sentences.zh: 生子魯元，有寵於世祖，而知外祖嵩已死，唯有三舅，每言於世祖，世祖為訪其舅。

translations.literal: She bore a son, Luyuan, who won favor with Emperor Shizu; knowing that his maternal grandfather Song was dead and that he had only three maternal uncles, he spoke of them often to the emperor, and the emperor sought out his uncles.
translations.idiomatic: She bore a son, Luyuan, who won Emperor Taiwu's favor; knowing his maternal grandfather Song was dead and that only three maternal uncles remained, he spoke of them often to the emperor, who then sought them out.

sentences.zh: 是時東方罕有仕者，廣、盆皆不樂入平城，洛齊獨請行，曰：「我養子，兼人道不全，當為兄弟試禍福也。

translations.literal: At that time few from the east took office; Guang and Pen were both unwilling to enter Pingcheng, but Luoqi alone asked to go, saying, "I am an adopted son, and moreover my humanity is incomplete; I ought to test fortune and misfortune for my brothers."
translations.idiomatic: Few easterners took office at court then; Guang and Pen were both reluctant to go to Pingcheng, but Luoqi alone volunteered, saying, "I am an adopted son, and my body is incomplete; let me go first and test fortune for my brothers."

sentences.zh: 」乃乘驢赴京。

translations.literal: " He then rode a donkey to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: " He then rode a donkey to the capital.

sentences.zh: 魯元候知將至，結從者百餘騎，迎于桑乾河，見而下拜，從者亦同致敬。

translations.literal: Luyuan, having learned he was coming, gathered more than a hundred mounted followers and met him at the Sanggan River; upon seeing him he bowed down, and his followers likewise paid their respects.
translations.idiomatic: Luyuan, hearing he was on his way, gathered more than a hundred mounted attendants and met him at the Sanggan River; he bowed upon seeing him, and his followers did the same.

sentences.zh: 入言于世祖，世祖問其才用所宜，將授之以官。

translations.literal: He entered and reported to Emperor Shizu; the emperor asked what talents and uses suited him and was about to grant him an office.
translations.idiomatic: He reported to Emperor Taiwu, who asked what office would suit his talents and was about to appoint him.

sentences.zh: 魯元曰：「臣舅不幸生為閹人，唯合與陛下守宮闈耳。

translations.literal: Luyuan said, "My uncle was unfortunately born a eunuch; he is fit only to guard the palace inner quarters for Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Luyuan said, "My uncle was unfortunately born a eunuch; he is fit only to guard the inner palace for Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」而不言其養子。

translations.literal: " He did not mention that he was an adopted son.
translations.idiomatic: " He did not mention that Luoqi was an adopted son.

sentences.zh: 世祖矜焉，賜以奴馬，引見。

translations.literal: The emperor took pity on him, granted him slaves and horses, and summoned him for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took pity on him, gave him slaves and horses, and received him in audience.

sentences.zh: 尋拜武衞將軍，俄而賜爵文安子，稍遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General of the Martial Guard; shortly afterward he was granted the title Marquis of Wen'an, and was gradually promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed General of the Martial Guard, then ennobled as Marquis of Wen'an, and later promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 魏初禁網疏闊，民戶隱匿漏脫者多。

translations.literal: In the early Wei the legal net was loose, and many households concealed themselves and escaped registration.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Northern Wei the laws were loosely enforced, and many households hid themselves to escape registration.

sentences.zh: 東州既平，綾羅戶民樂葵因是請採漏戶，供為綸綿。

translations.literal: After the eastern provinces were pacified, the silk-brocade household head Min Le requested on this basis to round up unregistered households to supply silk and floss.
translations.idiomatic: After the eastern provinces were pacified, Min Le, head of a silk-brocade household, requested permission to round up unregistered households to supply silk thread.

sentences.zh: 自後逃戶占為細繭羅縠者非一。

translations.literal: Afterward, fugitive households registered as fine-cocoon and gauze-brocade households were not few.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward many fugitive households were registered as fine-silk and gauze-brocade producers.

sentences.zh: [3]於是雜、營戶帥遍於天下，不屬守宰，發賦輕易，民多私附，戶口錯亂，不可檢括。

translations.literal: Thereupon heads of miscellaneous and camp households spread throughout the realm; they did not belong to local magistrates, levies were imposed lightly and easily, the people widely attached themselves privately, household registers fell into disorder, and they could not be checked or tallied.
translations.idiomatic: Heads of miscellaneous and camp households then spread throughout the realm; they answered to no local magistrate, levies were imposed at will, many people attached themselves privately to them, household registers fell into chaos, and the rolls could no longer be audited.

sentences.zh: 洛齊奏議罷之，一屬郡縣。

translations.literal: Luoqi memorialized proposing to abolish the practice and place all such households under the commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Luoqi memorialized to abolish the system and place all such households under county and commandery administration.

sentences.zh: 從平涼州，以功超遷散騎常侍，又加中書令、寧南將軍、進爵零陵公。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of Liang Province, for merit he was promoted beyond regular rank to Regular Attendant, then also made Director of the Secretariat, General Who Pacifies the South, and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the pacification of Liang Province and, for his merit, was promoted to Regular Attendant, then made Director of the Secretariat and General Who Pacifies the South and advanced to Duke of Lingling.

sentences.zh: 拜侍中、平遠將軍、冀州刺史，為內都大官。

translations.literal: He was appointed Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the Distance, and Governor of Ji Province, and served as Grand Officer of the Inner Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the Distance, and Governor of Ji Province, and served as Grand Officer of the Inner Capital.

sentences.zh: 興安二年卒，諡曰康。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Xing'an; his posthumous title was Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of the Xing'an era; his posthumous name was Kang.

sentences.zh: 養子儼，襲。

translations.literal: His adopted son Yan succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His adopted son Yan inherited his rank.

sentences.zh: 柔和敦敏，有長者風。

translations.literal: He was gentle, mild, and sincere in conduct, with the bearing of an elder.
translations.idiomatic: He was gentle, sincere, and dignified, with the bearing of a man of mature character.

sentences.zh: 太和中，為虎牢鎮將。

translations.literal: During the Taihe era he served as garrison commander of Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era he served as garrison commander of Hulao.

sentences.zh: 初洛齊貴盛之後，廣、盆坐他事誅，世祖以其非仇氏子，不與焉。

translations.literal: After Luoqi's rise to wealth and power, Guang and Pen were executed on other charges; Emperor Shizu, because they were not sons of the Chou clan, did not involve Yan.
translations.idiomatic: After Luoqi's rise to power, Guang and Pen were executed on other charges; Emperor Taiwu did not punish Yan, since he was not a Chou by blood.

sentences.zh: 還取侯家近屬，以儼為子。

translations.literal: He then took a close kinsman of the Hou family and made Yan his son.
translations.idiomatic: He then took a close kinsman of the Hou family and adopted Yan as his son.

sentences.zh: 後欲還本。

translations.literal: Later he wished to return to his original family.
translations.idiomatic: Later he wished to return to his birth family.

sentences.zh: 而廣有女孫配南安王楨，生章武王彬，即中山王英弟也。

translations.literal: Guang had a granddaughter who was married to Prince Nan'an Zhen and bore Prince Zhangwu Bin—who was the younger brother of Prince Zhongshan Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Guang had a granddaughter who married Prince Nan'an Zhen and bore Prince Zhangwu Bin, younger brother of Prince Zhongshan Ying.

sentences.zh: 仇妃聞而請儼曰：「由我仇家富貴至此，奈何一旦孤背恩養也！

translations.literal: The Chou consort, hearing of it, pleaded with Yan, saying, "It was through my Chou family that you rose to such wealth and honor—how can you suddenly turn your back alone on the grace of your upbringing!"
translations.idiomatic: The Chou consort, hearing of it, pleaded with Yan: "It was through my Chou family that you rose to such wealth and honor—how can you suddenly abandon the family that raised you!"

sentences.zh: 」楨時在內都主司品臣，儼隸於楨，畏憚之，遂不敢。

translations.literal: " At the time Zhen was chief officer in the Inner Capital overseeing ranked officials; Yan was subordinate to Zhen, feared and stood in awe of him, and therefore did not dare.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time Zhen headed the Inner Capital office that ranked officials; Yan was under his authority, feared him, and therefore did not dare.

sentences.zh: 九年卒，諡曰靜。

translations.literal: He died in the ninth year; his posthumous title was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year; his posthumous name was Jing.

sentences.zh: 子振襲。

translations.literal: His son Zhen succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen inherited his rank.

sentences.zh: 稍遷至中堅將軍、長水校尉。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to General of the Central Garrison and Colonel of the Long River.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to General of the Central Garrison and Colonel of the Long River.

sentences.zh: 廣、盆並善營產業，家于中山，號為巨富，子孫仕進至州主簿。

translations.literal: Guang and Pen were both skilled at building up estates; their family was established in Zhongshan and was called enormously wealthy; descendants entered office up to provincial chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Guang and Pen were both skilled at building estates; their family settled in Zhongshan and was renowned for vast wealth; descendants rose in office as high as provincial chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 騰曾孫儁，位至龍驤將軍、驍騎將軍、樂平男。

translations.literal: Teng's great-grandson Jun rose to General of the Dragon Cavalry, General of Valiant Cavalry, and Baron of Leping.
translations.idiomatic: Teng's great-grandson Jun rose to General of the Dragon Cavalry, General of Valiant Cavalry, and Baron of Leping.

sentences.zh: 段霸，雁門原平人。

translations.literal: Duan Ba was a man of Yuanping in Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ba was from Yuanping in Yanmen Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父乾，慕容垂廣武令。

translations.literal: His father Gan was magistrate of Guangwu under Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gan had been magistrate of Guangwu under Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 太祖初遣騎略地至雁門，霸年幼見執，因被宮刑。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor first sent cavalry to raid the territory as far as Yanmen, Ba was young and was seized; he therefore suffered palace castration.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor first sent cavalry to raid as far as Yanmen, the young Ba was captured and castrated.

sentences.zh: 乾尋率鄉部歸化雲中。

translations.literal: Gan soon led his township and district to submit and be naturalized at Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Gan soon led his township to submit and settle at Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 霸少以謹敏見知，稍遷至中常侍、中護軍將軍、殿中尚書，領壽安少府，賜爵武陵公。

translations.literal: Ba, while young, was known for prudence and alertness; he was gradually promoted to Regular Palace Attendant, General of the Central Guard, Director of the Palace Masters of Writing, concurrent head of the Shou'an Junior Household, and was granted the title Duke of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Ba was known from youth for prudence and alertness; he rose to Regular Palace Attendant, General of the Central Guard, and Director of the Palace Masters of Writing, concurrently headed the Shou'an Junior Household, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 出為安東將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 世祖親考內外，大明黜陟。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu personally examined inner and outer offices and made promotions and dismissals brilliantly clear.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu personally reviewed officials at court and in the provinces and made promotions and dismissals with unmistakable clarity.

sentences.zh: 前定州治中張渾屯告霸前在定州濁貨貪穢，便道致財，歸之鄉里。

translations.literal: The former chief clerk of Ding Province, Zhang Huntun, reported that Ba, while previously in Ding Province, had trafficked in illicit goods and been greedy and corrupt, used his official route to amass wealth, and sent it home to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: The former chief clerk of Ding Province, Zhang Huntun, reported that Ba, while governing Ding Province, had traded in contraband, taken bribes, used his official travel to amass wealth, and sent it home.

sentences.zh: 召霸定對，霸不首引。

translations.literal: Ba was summoned to answer the charges in person; he did not confess first.
translations.idiomatic: Ba was summoned to answer the charges but would not confess.

sentences.zh: 世祖以霸近臣而不盡實，由此益怒，欲斬之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Ba was a close attendant yet did not fully tell the truth, grew all the angrier on this account and wished to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Ba was a close attendant yet would not tell the whole truth, the emperor grew angrier and wanted to execute him.

sentences.zh: 恭宗進請，遂免霸為庶人。

translations.literal: Emperor Gong advanced to plead on his behalf, and Ba was thereupon stripped of office and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Gong pleaded on his behalf, and Ba was stripped of office and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 霸從弟榮，雍州別駕。

translations.literal: Ba's younger cousin Rong was Vice Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Ba's younger cousin Rong served as Vice Governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 兄弟諸從遂世居廣武城，修飾有士風。

translations.literal: The brothers and their cousins then dwelt for generations in Guangwu city, cultivating refinement with the air of scholar-gentry.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers and their cousins then settled for generations in Guangwu city, cultivating refinement in the manner of scholar-gentry families.

sentences.zh: 王琚，高平人，自云本太原人。

translations.literal: Wang Ju was a man of Gaoping; he himself said his family was originally from Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ju was from Gaoping; he claimed his family was originally from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 高祖始，晉豫州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozu's reign he was Governor of Yu Province under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the dynasty he had been Governor of Yu Province under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 琚以泰常中被刑入宮禁，小心守節，久乃見敍用。

translations.literal: Ju, because he was punished by castration during the Taichang era, entered the palace precincts; he was careful in keeping his integrity, and only after a long time was he employed in due order.
translations.idiomatic: Ju was castrated during the Taichang era and entered palace service; he served carefully and faithfully, and only after many years was he given office.

sentences.zh: 稍遷為禮部尚書，賜爵廣平公，加寧南將軍。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Minister of Rites, granted the title Duke of Guangping, and given the additional post of General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Minister of Rites, enfeoffed as Duke of Guangping, and made General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 高祖以琚歷奉先朝，志在公正，授散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu, because Ju had served through the previous reigns and aimed at fairness, appointed him Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Because Ju had served through earlier reigns with a reputation for fairness, Emperor Xiaowen appointed him Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 後為侍中、征南將車、冀州刺史，假廣平王。

translations.literal: Later he served as Palace Attendant, General Who Conquers the South, and Governor of Ji Province, with the provisional title Prince of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Palace Attendant, General Who Conquers the South, and Governor of Ji Province, with the provisional title Prince of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 徵還，進為征南將軍，進爵高平王，侍中如故，遣還冀州。

translations.literal: Recalled to court, he was advanced to General Who Conquers the South, promoted in enfeoffment to Prince of Gaoping, retained his post as Palace Attendant, and was sent back to Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was promoted to General Who Conquers the South and Prince of Gaoping, kept his post as Palace Attendant, and was sent back to Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 高祖、文明太后東巡冀州，親幸其家，存問周至。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenming toured Ji Province in the east, personally visited his home, and inquired after him with thorough care.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming toured Ji Province, they visited his home in person and inquired after him with exceptional care.

sentences.zh: 還京，以其年老，拜散騎常侍，養老於家。

translations.literal: On returning to the capital, because he was old, he was appointed Regular Attendant and allowed to retire and live at home.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the capital, he was appointed Regular Attendant and allowed to retire at home because of his age.

sentences.zh: 前後賜以車馬衣服雜物不可稱計。

translations.literal: Before and after, he was granted carriages, horses, clothing, and miscellaneous goods beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Over the years he received countless gifts of carriages, horses, clothing, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 後降爵為公，扶老自平城從遷洛邑。

translations.literal: Later his rank was reduced to duke; leaning on his staff, he followed the move from Pingcheng to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later his title was reduced to duke; leaning on his staff, he followed the court's move from Pingcheng to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖以其朝舊，遣左右勞問之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu, because he was an elder of the court, sent attendants to express sympathy and inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was a veteran of the court, Emperor Xiaowen sent attendants to visit and comfort him.

sentences.zh: 琚附表自陳初至家多乏，蒙賜帛二百匹。

translations.literal: Ju submitted a memorial stating that since he first arrived home he had been much in want, and received a grant of two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Ju submitted a memorial saying that since returning home he had been in want, and received two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 常飲牛乳，色如處子。

translations.literal: He regularly drank cow's milk, and his complexion was like that of a maiden.
translations.idiomatic: He drank cow's milk regularly, and his complexion remained as fresh as a young woman's.

sentences.zh: 太和二十年冬卒，時年九十。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twentieth year of Taihe, he died; at the time he was ninety years old.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the winter of the twentieth year of Taihe (496), at the age of ninety.

sentences.zh: 贈征南將軍、冀州刺史，諡曰靖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted General Who Conquers the South and Inspector of Ji Province; his posthumous name was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as General Who Conquers the South and Inspector of Ji Province, with the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 養子寄生，未襲而亡。

translations.literal: His adopted son Jisheng died before inheriting the title.
translations.idiomatic: His adopted son Jisheng died before he could inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 子蓋海，襲祖琚爵。

translations.literal: His son Gaihai inherited his grandfather Ju's title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gaihai inherited the title of his grandfather Ju.

sentences.zh: 初琚年七十餘，賜得世祖時宮人郭氏，本鍾離人，明嚴有母德，內外婦孫百口，奉之肅若嚴君，家內以治。

translations.literal: In the beginning, when Ju was over seventy, he was granted the palace woman Guo from the reign of Emperor Shizu; she was originally from Zhongli. Stern and bright, she possessed motherly virtue; among the hundred mouths of women and grandchildren inside and outside the household, all served her with the solemnity due a strict matriarch, and the household was thereby well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: When Ju was in his seventies, he was granted a palace woman of the name Guo from the Taiwu era. A native of Zhongli, she was stern yet virtuous as a mother figure. The hundred-odd women and grandchildren of the household treated her with the reverence owed a household head, and under her the family was well run.

sentences.zh: 蓋海官至青州樂陵太守。

translations.literal: Gaihai reached the office of Administrator of Leiling in Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Gaihai rose to the post of Administrator of Leiling in Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 趙黑，字文靜，初名海，本涼州隸戶。

translations.literal: Zhao He, styled Wenjing, originally named Hai, was originally a dependent household of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao He, courtesy name Wenjing, originally named Hai, came from a dependent household in Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 自云其先河內溫人也，五世祖術，晉末為平遠將軍、西夷校尉，因居酒泉安彌縣。

translations.literal: He himself said his ancestors were from Wen in Henei; his fifth-generation ancestor Shu, at the end of Jin, served as General Who Pacifies the Distance and Commandant of Western Barbarians, and thereby settled in Anmi County, Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed descent from Wen in Henei. His fifth-generation ancestor Shu served in the late Jin as General Who Pacifies the Distance and Commandant of the Western Barbarians, and settled in Anmi County in Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 海生而涼州平，沒入為閹人，因改名為黑。

translations.literal: Hai was born just as Liang Province was pacified; he was castrated and became a eunuch, and therefore changed his name to Hei (Black).
translations.idiomatic: Hai was born just as Liang Province was pacified. He was castrated and entered palace service as a eunuch, and thereafter took the name Hei (Black).

sentences.zh: 有容貌，恭謹小心。

translations.literal: He had good looks and was respectful, careful, and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: He was handsome and conducted himself with respectful care.

sentences.zh: 世祖使進御膳，出入承奉，初無過行。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu had him serve the imperial meals; going in and out in attendance, at first he had no misconduct.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu put him in charge of serving the imperial meals. Attending the emperor in and out of court, he initially committed no fault.

sentences.zh: 遷侍御，典監藏，拜安遠將軍，賜爵睢陽侯。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant at Court, supervised the treasury, was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance, and granted the title Marquis of Suiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace attendant, put in charge of the treasury, made General Who Pacifies the Distance, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Suiyang.

sentences.zh: 轉選部尚書，能自謹厲，當官任舉，頗得其人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Personnel Bureau; able to restrain himself with strictness, when holding office and making appointments, he obtained quite suitable men.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel. Self-disciplined and strict, he made appointments that generally brought the right men to office.

sentences.zh: 加侍中，進爵河內公。

translations.literal: He was given the additional post of Palace Attendant and advanced in rank to Duke of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Palace Attendant and promoted to Duke of Henei.

sentences.zh: 顯祖將傳位京兆王子推，訪諸羣臣，百官唯唯，莫敢先言者，唯源賀等詞義正直，不肯奉詔。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu was about to pass the throne to Prince Tui of Jingzhao; he consulted the various ministers, and the hundred officials equivocated—none dared speak first. Only Yuan He and others spoke with upright principle and refused to obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzu was about to abdicate in favor of Prince Tui of Jingzhao, he consulted his ministers. The officials all mumbled assent, and none dared speak up first. Only Yuan He and a few others spoke plainly and refused to obey the edict.

sentences.zh: 顯祖怒，變色，復以問黑。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu grew angry, his expression changed, and he questioned He again.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu grew angry, his face darkened, and he put the question to He once more.

sentences.zh: 黑曰：「臣愚無識，信情率意。

translations.literal: He said: "Your subject is foolish and without understanding; I speak according to my sincere feelings and straightforward intent.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Your subject is dull and ignorant, and speaks only from sincere conviction.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下春秋始富，如日方中，天下說其盛明，萬物懷其光景，元元之心，願終萬歲。

translations.literal: Considering that Your Majesty's years are just flourishing, like the sun at midday; all under heaven praise your brilliant governance, the ten thousand things cherish your radiance, and the common people's hearts wish you ten thousand years to the end.
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty is still in the prime of life, like the sun at noon. The realm praises your brilliance, all creation basks in your glory, and the people wish you long life.

sentences.zh: 若聖性淵遠，欲頤神味道者，臣黑以死奉戴皇太子，不知其他。

translations.literal: If Your Sage Majesty's nature is profound and far-reaching and you wish to nourish your spirit and savor the Way, your subject Hei would die to support and uphold the Crown Prince—I know nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: "If Your Majesty's sage nature runs deep and you wish to retire and cultivate the Way, this subject Hei would give his life to serve the Crown Prince—and knows nothing beyond that.

sentences.zh: 」顯祖默然良久，遂傳祚于高祖。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu was silent for a long while, and then passed the imperial throne to Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu fell silent for a long time, then passed the throne to Emperor Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 黑得幸兩宮，祿賜優厚。

translations.literal: He gained favor in both palaces, and his salary and gifts were generous.
translations.idiomatic: He enjoyed favor in both palaces, and received lavish salaries and gifts.

sentences.zh: 是時尚書李訢亦有寵於顯祖，與黑對綰選部。

translations.literal: At that time the Minister Li Xin also had favor with Emperor Xianzu, and together with He jointly oversaw the Personnel Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Minister Li Xin was also favored by Emperor Xianzu, and he shared oversight of the Personnel Bureau with He.

sentences.zh: 訢奏中書侍郎崔鑒為東徐州，北部主書郎公孫處顯為荊州，選部監公孫蘧為幽州，皆曰有能也，實有私焉。

translations.literal: Xin memorialized to appoint Assistant in the Central Secretariat Cui Jian as Inspector of Eastern Xuzhou, Northern Bureau Chief Clerk Gongsun Chuxian as Inspector of Jing Province, and Personnel Bureau Supervisor Gongsun Qu as Inspector of You Province—all were said to be capable, but in fact there was private motive.
translations.idiomatic: Xin recommended Central Secretariat Assistant Cui Jian for Eastern Xuzhou, Northern Bureau Chief Clerk Gongsun Chuxian for Jing Province, and Personnel Supervisor Gongsun Qu for You Province—all allegedly for their ability, but in fact out of favoritism.

sentences.zh: 黑疾其虧亂選體，遂爭於殿庭曰：「以功授官，因爵與祿，國之常典。

translations.literal: He resented this undermining and disorder of the selection system, and therefore argued in the palace hall, saying: "Awarding office by merit and granting salary by rank is the state's regular principle.
translations.idiomatic: He resented this corruption of the selection system and challenged Xin in open court: "Offices should go to the meritorious and salaries to the ennobled—this is the state's established law.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎、尚書主書郎、諸曹監，勳能俱立，不過列郡，今訢皆用為方州，臣實為惑。

translations.literal: Assistants in the Central Secretariat, chief clerks of the ministries, and supervisors of the various bureaus—even with both merit and ability established, at most reach a commandery rank; now Xin uses them all as provincial inspectors, and your subject is truly puzzled.
translations.idiomatic: "Central Secretariat assistants, ministry chief clerks, and bureau supervisors—even at their best reach no higher than commandery posts. Yet Xin has made them all provincial governors. I am genuinely baffled.

sentences.zh: 」顯祖疑之，曰：「公孫蘧且止。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu was suspicious and said, "Hold Gongsun Qu for now."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu was uncertain and said, "Hold Gongsun Qu's appointment for now."

sentences.zh: 」蘧最為訢厚，於是黑與訢遂為深隙。

translations.literal: Qu was closest to Xin in affection, and so He and Xin thus became deeply estranged.
translations.idiomatic: Qu was Xin's closest ally, and from that day He and Xin became bitter enemies.

sentences.zh: 訢竟列黑為監藏時多所截沒。

translations.literal: Xin ultimately charged that when He oversaw the treasury he had embezzled much.
translations.idiomatic: Xin eventually accused He of widespread embezzlement during his tenure overseeing the treasury.

sentences.zh: 先是法禁寬緩，百司所典，與官並食，故多所損折。

translations.literal: Previously the laws were lenient; what the hundred offices administered they shared meals with officials, and therefore there was much loss and damage.
translations.idiomatic: The laws had previously been lax: offices shared their perquisites with their officials, so losses were common.

sentences.zh: 遂黜為門士。

translations.literal: He was thereupon demoted to a gate guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to the rank of gate guard.

sentences.zh: 黑自以為訢所陷，歎恨終日，廢寢忘食，規報前怨。

translations.literal: He believed himself framed by Xin; sighing with resentment all day, he forgot sleep and food, plotting to repay the old grievance.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced he had been framed by Xin, he brooded all day, sleepless and without appetite, plotting revenge.

sentences.zh: 踰年，還入為侍御、散騎常侍、侍中、尚書左僕射，復兼選部如昔。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was recalled and served as Attendant at Court, Regular Attendant, Palace Attendant, and Left Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs, again concurrently holding the Personnel Bureau as before.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he was recalled as palace attendant, Regular Attendant, Palace Attendant, and Left Vice Minister of Affairs, and again held the Personnel Bureau as before.

sentences.zh: 黑告訢專恣，訢遂出為徐州。

translations.literal: He reported that Xin was arbitrary and willful, and Xin was thereupon sent out as Inspector of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He denounced Xin for abusing his power, and Xin was sent out as Inspector of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 及其將獲罪也，黑構成以誅之。

translations.literal: When Xin was about to be punished, He framed him and had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xin was on the verge of punishment, He engineered his condemnation and had him put to death.

sentences.zh: 然後食甘寢安，志在於職事。

translations.literal: Only then did he eat sweetly and sleep peacefully, with his mind set on official duties.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did he eat and sleep in peace, turning his full attention to his duties.

sentences.zh: 出為假節、鎮南大將軍、儀同三司、定州刺史，進爵為王。

translations.literal: He was sent out with provisional credentials as Great General Who Guards the South, Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes, and Inspector of Ding Province, and advanced in rank to king.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as commissioner with full authority, Great General Who Guards the South, Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes, and Inspector of Ding Province, and was promoted to king.

sentences.zh: 克己清儉，憂濟公私。

translations.literal: He restrained himself, was pure and frugal, and cared for both public and private needs.
translations.idiomatic: He was self-restrained, frugal, and devoted to easing the burdens of both the state and the people.

sentences.zh: 時有人欲行私賂，黑曰：「高官祿厚，足以自給，賣公營私，本非情願。

translations.literal: At the time someone wished to offer a private bribe; He said: "High rank and thick salary are enough for self-support; selling public office for private gain was never my wish.
translations.idiomatic: When someone tried to bribe him privately, He said: "My high office and generous salary are enough to live on. Trading public duty for private gain has never been my intention.

sentences.zh: 」終無所納。

translations.literal: In the end he accepted nothing.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he accepted nothing.

sentences.zh: 高祖、文明太后幸中山，聞之，賜帛五百匹、穀一千五百石。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenming visited Zhongshan; hearing of this, they granted five hundred bolts of silk and fifteen hundred shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming visited Zhongshan and heard of this, they granted him five hundred bolts of silk and fifteen hundred shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 轉冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Inspector of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 太和六年秋薨於官。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the sixth year of Taihe he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the autumn of the sixth year of Taihe (482).

sentences.zh: 詔賜絹四百五十匹、穀一千斛、車牛二十乘，致柩至都。

translations.literal: An edict granted four hundred fifty bolts of silk, one thousand hu of grain, and twenty pairs of ox-carts, and had the coffin conveyed to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted four hundred fifty bolts of silk, a thousand hu of grain, and twenty ox-cart teams to convey his coffin to the capital.

sentences.zh: 追贈司空公，諡曰康。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted Duke of Works; his posthumous name was Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Works, with the posthumous name Kang.

sentences.zh: 黑養族弟趙奴第四子熾為後。

translations.literal: He adopted as heir the fourth son Chi of his clansman Zhao Nu.
translations.idiomatic: He adopted as his heir Chi, the fourth son of his clansman Zhao Nu.

sentences.zh: 熾，字貴樂。

translations.literal: Chi, styled Guile.
translations.idiomatic: Chi, courtesy name Guile.

sentences.zh: 初為中散，襲黑爵，後降為公。

translations.literal: Initially he served as Central University graduate; he inherited He's title, and later was reduced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a Central University graduate, inherited He's title, and was later reduced to duke.

sentences.zh: 官至揚州安南府長史，加平遠將軍。

translations.literal: He reached the office of Chief Administrator of An'nan Prefecture in Yang Province, with the additional post of General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Chief Administrator of An'nan Prefecture in Yang Province and was made General Who Pacifies the Distance.

sentences.zh: 元嵩之死壽春也，熾處分安輯，微有聲稱。

translations.literal: When Yuan Song died at Shouchun, Chi managed affairs and brought calm, gaining a slight reputation.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Song died at Shouchun, Chi took charge and restored order, winning a modest reputation.

sentences.zh: 神龜中卒，贈光州刺史。

translations.literal: He died during the Shengui era and was posthumously granted Inspector of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Shengui era and was posthumously made Inspector of Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 黑為定州，與熾納鉅鹿魏幹女，有二子。

translations.literal: When He was at Ding Province, he and Chi took in marriage the daughter of Wei Gan of Julu, and had two sons.
translations.idiomatic: While He served at Ding Province, he and Chi married the daughter of Wei Gan of Julu, and they had two sons.

sentences.zh: 長子揆，字景則。

translations.literal: The eldest son Kui, styled Jingze.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son was Kui, courtesy name Jingze.

sentences.zh: 襲父侯爵，官至樂陵太守。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's marquisate and reached the office of Administrator of Leiling.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's marquisate and rose to Administrator of Leiling.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈左將軍、滄州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Left General and Inspector of Cang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Left General and Inspector of Cang Province.

sentences.zh: 揆弟儁之，字仲彥，輕薄無行。

translations.literal: Kui's younger brother Junzhi, styled Zhongyan, was frivolous and without proper conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Kui's younger brother Junzhi, courtesy name Zhongyan, was frivolous and dissolute.

sentences.zh: 為給事中，轉謁者僕射，為劉騰養息。

translations.literal: He served as Supervising Censor, was transferred to Director of the Gate, and became the adopted son of Liu Teng.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Supervising Censor, then Director of the Gate, and was adopted as a son by Liu Teng.

sentences.zh: 猶以閹官餘資，賂遺權門，頻歷顯官而卒。

translations.literal: Still relying on eunuch residual resources, he bribed powerful families, repeatedly held prominent offices, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on the residual wealth of eunuch office, he bribed the powerful, rose repeatedly to high posts, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 孫小，字茂翹，咸陽石安人。

translations.literal: Sun Xiao, styled Maoqiao, was a native of Shi'an in Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiao, courtesy name Maoqiao, was from Shi'an in Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 父瓚，姚泓安定護軍。

translations.literal: His father Zan was Protector General of Anding under Yao Hong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zan served as Protector General of Anding under Yao Hong.

sentences.zh: 為赫連屈丐所侵，人懷危懼，亡奔者相屬，瓚獨率眾拒守，見殺。

translations.literal: Invaded by Helian Qubug, the people were filled with fear and those fleeing in succession were unbroken; Zan alone led the multitude in resistance and defense, and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Helian Qubug invaded, the people were terrified and refugees streamed away. Zan alone led his troops in defense and was killed.

sentences.zh: 小沒入宮刑。

translations.literal: Xiao underwent palace castration.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao was castrated and entered palace service.

sentences.zh: 會魏平統萬，遂徙平城，內侍東宮。

translations.literal: When Wei pacified Tongwan, he was thereupon moved to Pingcheng and served internally in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei captured Tongwan, he was moved to Pingcheng and assigned to serve in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 以聰識有智略稱。

translations.literal: He was known for intelligence, discernment, and strategic ability.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for his intelligence and strategic ability.

sentences.zh: 未幾，轉西臺中散，每從征伐，屢有戰功，多獲賞賜。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Central University graduate of the Western Platform; each time he followed on campaigns he repeatedly won battle merit and received many rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made a Central University graduate of the Western Platform. He followed the army on campaign, won repeated honors in battle, and received many rewards.

sentences.zh: 世祖幸瓜步，慮有北寇之虞，乃加小左衞將軍，賜爵泥陽子，除留臺將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu visited Guabu, fearing concern over northern invaders, he thereupon added to Xiao the post of Left Guard General, granted the title Baron of Niyang, and appointed him Capital Garrison General.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu visited Guabu, anxious about a northern attack, he made Xiao Left Guard General, enfeoffed him as Baron of Niyang, and appointed him Capital Garrison General.

sentences.zh: 車駕還都，遷給事中，綰太僕曹。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, he was promoted to Supervising Censor and oversaw the Ministry of Parks.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, he was promoted to Supervising Censor and put in charge of the Ministry of Parks.

sentences.zh: 乃請父瓚贈諡，求更改葬，詔贈振威將軍、秦州刺史、石安縣子，諡曰戴。

translations.literal: He then requested a posthumous grant of title and posthumous name for his father Zan and asked for reburial; an edict granted General Who Quells Might, Inspector of Qin Province, and Baron of Shi'an County, with posthumous name Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned for a posthumous title and reburial for his father Zan. An edict granted Zan the post of General Who Quells Might, Inspector of Qin Province, and Baron of Shi'an County, with the posthumous name Dai.

sentences.zh: 轉小領駕部，課理有方，畜牧蕃息。

translations.literal: He was transferred to minor Director of the Chariot Department; his assessment and management were effective, and livestock multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: He was made minor Director of the Chariot Department. His management was effective, and the herds prospered.

sentences.zh: 出為冠軍將軍、并州刺史，進爵中都侯，州內四郡百餘人詣闕頌其政化。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Champion General and Inspector of Bing Province, advanced to Marquis of Zhongdu; more than a hundred people from four commanderies within the province came to the palace gate to praise his governance and transformation.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Champion General and Inspector of Bing Province and was promoted to Marquis of Zhongdu. More than a hundred men from four commanderies came to court to praise his governance.

sentences.zh: 後遷冀州刺史，聲稱微少於前。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Inspector of Ji Province; his reputation was slightly less than before.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Inspector of Ji Province, his reputation fell slightly short of what it had been.

sentences.zh: 然所在清約，當時牧伯無能及也。

translations.literal: Yet wherever he served he was pure and frugal; no regional governor of the time could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet wherever he served he was austere and frugal—no provincial governor of the day could equal him.

sentences.zh: 性頗忍酷，所養子息，驅馳鞭撻，視如仇讎。

translations.literal: His nature was rather cruel; the sons he had adopted he drove and whipped, treating them like sworn enemies.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature harsh and cruel, driving and beating the sons he had adopted as though they were mortal enemies.

sentences.zh: 小之為并州，以郭祚為主簿，重祚門才，兼任之以書記，時人多之。

translations.literal: When Xiao was at Bing Province, he made Guo Zuo chief clerk, valued Zuo's family talent, and concurrently entrusted him with secretarial duties; many at the time praised this.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao served at Bing Province, he made Guo Zuo his chief clerk. Valuing Zuo's family talent, he also put him in charge of correspondence—a choice widely admired at the time.

sentences.zh: 張宗之，字益宗，河南鞏人，家世寒微。

translations.literal: Zhang Zongzhi, styled Yizong, was a native of Gong in Henan; his family for generations was humble and lowly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zongzhi, courtesy name Yizong, was from Gong in Henan. His family had been humble for generations.

sentences.zh: 父孟舒，劉裕西征，假洛陽令。

translations.literal: His father Mengshu, when Liu Yu marched west, was appointed acting Magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mengshu served as acting Magistrate of Luoyang during Liu Yu's western campaign.

sentences.zh: 及宗之貴幸，高宗贈孟舒平南將軍、洛州刺史、鞏縣侯，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: When Zongzhi became honored and favored, Emperor Gaozong posthumously granted Mengshu General Who Pacifies the South, Inspector of Luo Province, and Marquis of Gong County, with posthumous name Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongzhi rose to power, Emperor Wencheng posthumously enfeoffed Mengshu as General Who Pacifies the South, Inspector of Luo Province, and Marquis of Gong County, with the posthumous name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 初緱氏宗文邕聚黨於伊闕謀反，逼脅孟舒等。

translations.literal: Initially Zong Wen'ao of the Gou clan gathered a faction at Yique to plot rebellion and coerced Mengshu and others.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, Zong Wen'ao of Gou gathered rebels at Yique and forced Mengshu and others to join them.

sentences.zh: 文邕敗，孟舒走免，宗之被執入京，充腐刑。

translations.literal: Wen'ao was defeated; Mengshu fled and escaped, and Zongzhi was seized and brought to the capital, where he underwent castration.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen'ao was defeated, Mengshu fled and escaped. Zongzhi was captured and sent to the capital, where he was castrated.

sentences.zh: 以忠厚謹慎，擢為侍御中散，賜爵鞏縣侯，遂歷右將軍，中常侍，[4]儀曹、庫部二曹尚書，領中祕書，進爵彭城公。

translations.literal: For loyalty, honesty, and prudence, he was promoted to Attendant Central University graduate, granted the title Marquis of Gong County, and then successively served as Right General, Regular Palace Attendant, Minister of the Ceremonies and Treasury bureaus, Overseer of the Central Secretariat, and advanced to Duke of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: For his loyalty and prudence he was promoted to palace attendant and Central University graduate, enfeoffed as Marquis of Gong County, and rose through the posts of Right General, Regular Palace Attendant, Minister of the Ceremonies and Treasury bureaus, and Overseer of the Central Secretariat, eventually becoming Duke of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 出為散騎常侍、寧西將軍、東雍州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Eastern Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Eastern Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 以在官有稱，入為內都大官。

translations.literal: Because he had a good reputation in office, he was recalled as Grand Director of Internal Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: For his reputation in office he was recalled as Grand Director of Internal Affairs.

sentences.zh: 出除散騎常侍、鎮東將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out to serve as Regular Attendant, General Who Guards the East, and Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out again as Regular Attendant, General Who Guards the East, and Inspector of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 又例降為侯。

translations.literal: He was again reduced to marquis by regulation.
translations.idiomatic: His title was again reduced to marquis under the usual regulations.

sentences.zh: 太和二十年卒，年六十九，贈建節將軍、懷州刺史，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Taihe he died at age sixty-nine; he was posthumously granted General with Staff of Authority, Inspector of Huai Province, with posthumous name Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twentieth year of Taihe (496) at sixty-nine. He was posthumously made General with Staff of Authority and Inspector of Huai Province, with the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 宗之兄鸞旗，中書侍郎、東宮中庶子，兼宿衞給事。

translations.literal: Zongzhi's older brother Luanqi served as Assistant in the Central Secretariat, Junior Tutor of the Eastern Palace, and concurrently Night Guard Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhi's elder brother Luanqi served as Central Secretariat Assistant, Junior Tutor of the Eastern Palace, and concurrently as a night-guard attendant.

sentences.zh: 加寧遠將軍，賜爵洛陽男。

translations.literal: He was given the additional post of General Who Pacifies the Distance and granted the title Baron of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General Who Pacifies the Distance and enfeoffed as Baron of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 轉殿中給事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant in the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 出為散騎常侍、冠軍將軍、涇州刺史，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Regular Attendant, Champion General, and Inspector of Jing Province, and advanced in rank to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Regular Attendant, Champion General, and Inspector of Jing Province, and was promoted to marquis.

sentences.zh: 復為殿中給事、中常侍。

translations.literal: He again served as Attendant in the Palace and Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as palace attendant and Regular Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈洛州刺史，諡曰靖。

translations.literal: He died; he was posthumously granted Inspector of Luo Province, with posthumous name Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Inspector of Luo Province, with the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 始宗之納南來殷孝祖妻蕭氏，劉義隆儀同三司思話弟思度女也，多悉婦人儀飾故事。

translations.literal: Initially Zongzhi took in marriage the wife of Yin Xiaozu who had come from the south, the Lady Xiao—daughter of Sihua's brother Sidu, who held Equal in Rank to Three Dukes under Liu Yilong—and she knew much of women's ceremonial dress and customs of old.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhi had married the wife of the southern defector Yin Xiaozu, a Lady Xiao who was the daughter of Sidu, brother of Liu Yilong's Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes Sihua. She knew a great deal about women's ceremonial dress and customs.

sentences.zh: 太和中，初制六宮服章，蕭被命在內預見訪採，數蒙賜賚。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, when the dress insignia of the six palaces were first established, Xiao was commanded to participate inside in advance consultation and inquiry, and repeatedly received gifts.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe reforms, when the dress codes of the six palaces were first established, Lady Xiao was summoned to advise from within the palace and received many imperial gifts.

sentences.zh: 蕭兄子超業，後名彥，幼隨姑入國。

translations.literal: Xiao's elder brother's son Chaoye, later named Yan, as a child followed his aunt into the state.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xiao's nephew Chaoye, who later took the name Yan, came to Wei as a child with his aunt.

sentences.zh: 娶李洪之女，賴其給贍以自濟。

translations.literal: He married the daughter of Li Hong and relied on her provision and support to sustain himself.
translations.idiomatic: He married a daughter of Li Hong and lived on her family's support.

sentences.zh: 歷位太尉長史、武衞將軍、齊州刺史、散騎常侍、中軍將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Chief Administrator of the Grand Commandant, Martial Guard General, Inspector of Qi Province, Regular Attendant, Central Army General, and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Chief Administrator to the Grand Commandant, Martial Guard General, Inspector of Qi Province, Regular Attendant, Central Army General, and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle.

sentences.zh: 彥時來往蕭寶夤，致敬稱名，呼之為尊。

translations.literal: Yan at times visited Xiao Baoyin, showing respect and calling him by name, addressing him as "Lord."
translations.idiomatic: Yan frequently visited Xiao Baoyin, showing deference and addressing him by his personal name, calling him "my lord."

sentences.zh: 彥於河陰遇害，贈車騎將軍、儀同三司、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Yan met with disaster and was killed at Heyin; he was posthumously granted General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Rank to Three Dukes, and Inspector of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was killed at Heyin and was posthumously made General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes, and Inspector of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 子百年，西河太守。

translations.literal: His son Bainian was Administrator of Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bainian served as Administrator of Xihe.

sentences.zh: 宗之養兄子襲紹爵。

translations.literal: Zongzhi adopted his elder brother's son Xi to inherit the title.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhi adopted his elder brother's son Xi to inherit his title.

sentences.zh: 襲，字子業。

translations.literal: Xi, styled Ziye.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, courtesy name Ziye.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，除主文中散，稍遷員外郎，京兆王大農。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozu's reign, he was appointed Principal Writer Palace Attendant; gradually he was promoted to Supernumerary Cadet and Grand Agriculture Officer to the Prince of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Xi was made Principal Writer Palace Attendant, then gradually promoted to Supernumerary Cadet and Grand Agriculture Officer to the Prince of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 久之，除義陽太守，為司空劉騰諮議參軍、散騎常侍、平東將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was appointed Administrator of Yiyang, and served as Staff Advisor to the Secretariat of the Excellency of Works Liu Teng, Regular Attendant, Pacifier of the East General, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later he was appointed Administrator of Yiyang and served as Staff Advisor to Liu Teng, the Excellency of Works, while also holding the posts of Regular Attendant, Pacifier of the East General, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 太昌初卒，年七十七。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he died, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the beginning of the Taichang era, at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted General of Swift Cavalry, Equal in Rank to Three Dukes, and Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General of Swift Cavalry, Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes, and Inspector of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 子顥，邵郡太守。

translations.literal: His son Hao was Administrator of Shao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hao served as Administrator of Shao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; he was posthumously granted Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Inspector of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 顥弟璟，中散大夫。

translations.literal: Hao's younger brother Jing was a Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's younger brother Jing held the post of Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 璟弟瑋，武定中，豫州征西府長史。

translations.literal: Jing's younger brother Wei, in the Wuding era, was Chief Administrator of the Pacification of the West headquarters in Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's younger brother Wei served in the Wuding era as Chief Administrator of the Pacification of the West headquarters in Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 諸中官皆世衰，唯趙黑及宗之後，家僮數百，通於士流。

translations.literal: All the palace eunuchs saw their families decline in successive generations; only Zhao Hei and Zongzhi's descendants had several hundred household slaves and mingled with the scholar-official class.
translations.idiomatic: The great eunuch families all declined over the generations, but Zhao Hei and Zhang Zongzhi's line kept several hundred retainers and moved freely among the gentry.

sentences.zh: 劇鵬，高陽人。

translations.literal: Ju Peng was a man of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Peng was from Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 粗覽經史，閑曉吏事。

translations.literal: He had a rough survey of the classics and histories and was skilled and familiar with administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He had a rough grounding in the classics and histories and was well versed in administration.

sentences.zh: 與王質等俱充宦官，性通率，不以閽閹為耻。

translations.literal: Together with Wang Zhi and others he was appointed a palace eunuch; his nature was open and direct, and he did not take shame in being a gate-palace castrato.
translations.idiomatic: He entered palace service as a eunuch alongside Wang Zhi and others. Frank by nature, he did not feel ashamed of his status at the gate-palace.

sentences.zh: 文明太后時，亦見眷遇，為給事中。

translations.literal: In Empress Dowager Wenming's time he too received favor, and was made Attendant Within.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Dowager Wenming he also won favor and was appointed Attendant Within.

sentences.zh: 高祖遷洛，常為宮官，事幽后。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu moved the capital to Luoyang, he constantly served as a palace official attending Empress You.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang, he remained a palace official in the service of Empress You.

sentences.zh: 后之惑薩菩薩也，[5]鵬密諫止之，不從，遂發憤而卒。

translations.literal: When the empress was bewitched by Sa Pusa, Peng secretly remonstrated to stop it; she did not heed him, and he thereupon died in indignation.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress fell under the spell of the monk Sa Pusa, Peng secretly urged her to stop; she refused to listen, and he died of grief and anger.

sentences.zh: 兄買奴，亦為宦者。

translations.literal: His elder brother Mainu was also a eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Mainu was also a eunuch.

sentences.zh: 歷位幽州刺史。

translations.literal: He successively held the post of Inspector of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to serve as Inspector of You Province.

sentences.zh: 才志遠不及鵬。

translations.literal: His talent and resolve fell far short of Peng's.
translations.idiomatic: His ability and ambition were far inferior to Peng's.

sentences.zh: 是時有李豐之徒數人，[6]皆被眷寵，出入禁闈，並致名位，積貲巨萬，第宅華壯。

translations.literal: At that time there were several men such as Li Feng, all receiving favor and trust, entering and leaving the forbidden inner quarters, all attaining fame and rank, amassing wealth in the tens of thousands, with residences splendid and imposing.
translations.idiomatic: At that time several men such as Li Feng enjoyed imperial favor, came and went through the inner palaces, attained high rank, amassed enormous wealth, and built lavish mansions.

sentences.zh: 文明太后崩後，乃漸衰矣。

translations.literal: After Empress Dowager Wenming died, they gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Dowager Wenming's death, their fortunes gradually waned.

sentences.zh: 張祐，字安福，安定石唐人。

translations.literal: Zhang You, styled Anfu, was a man of Shitang in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang You, courtesy name Anfu, was from Shitang in Anding.

sentences.zh: 父成，扶風太守。

translations.literal: His father Cheng was Administrator of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cheng was Administrator of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 世祖末，坐事誅，祐充腐刑。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Shizu's reign, for a crime his father was executed, and You underwent castration.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Taiwu's reign his father was executed for a crime, and You was castrated.

sentences.zh: 積勞至曹監、中給事，賜爵黎陽男。

translations.literal: Through accumulated service he reached Supervisor of the Internal Directorate and Attendant Within, and was granted the title Baron of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Through long service he rose to Supervisor of the Internal Directorate and Attendant Within, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 稍遷散騎常侍，都綰內藏曹。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Regular Attendant and put in charge of the Inner Storehouse Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Regular Attendant and placed in charge of the Inner Storehouse Directorate.

sentences.zh: 時文明太后臨朝，中官用事。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Wenming held court, and palace eunuchs wielded power.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Empress Dowager Wenming held court, and eunuchs controlled affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 祐以左右供承合旨，寵幸冠諸閹官，特遷為尚書，加安南將軍，進爵隴東公，[7]仍綰內藏曹。

translations.literal: You, through attending at the ruler's side and meeting their wishes, enjoyed favor surpassing all the gate castrates; he was specially promoted to Master of Writing, with added General Who Pacifies the South, and advanced to Duke of Longdong, still heading the Inner Storehouse Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Attending at the ruler's side and anticipating every wish, You became the most favored of all the eunuchs. He was specially promoted to Master of Writing and General Who Pacifies the South, advanced to Duke of Longdong, while still heading the Inner Storehouse Directorate.

sentences.zh: 未幾，監都曹，加侍中，與王叡等俱入八議。

translations.literal: Before long he supervised the Directorate of Masters of Writing, was given the added title Chamberlain, and together with Wang Rui and others entered the Eight Deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he supervised the Directorate of Masters of Writing, was made Chamberlain, and together with Wang Rui and others joined the Eight Deliberations.

sentences.zh: 太后嘉其忠誠，為造甲宅。

translations.literal: The empress dowager praised his loyalty and sincerity and had a residence built for him.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager praised his loyalty and had a mansion built for him.

sentences.zh: 宅成，高祖、太后親率文武往燕會焉。

translations.literal: When the residence was completed, Emperor Gaozu and the empress dowager personally led civil and military officials there for a banquet assembly.
translations.idiomatic: When the mansion was finished, Emperor Xiaowen and the empress dowager personally led court officials there for a banquet.

sentences.zh: 拜散騎常侍、鎮南將軍、尚書左僕射，進爵新平王，受職于太華庭，備威儀於宮城之南，觀者以為榮。

translations.literal: He was appointed Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the South, and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; he was advanced to Prince of Xinping; he received office at Taihua Court, with full regalia south of the palace wall, and onlookers considered it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the South, and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and was advanced to Prince of Xinping. He received his commission at Taihua Court with full ceremonial in the south of the palace city, and the crowds who watched considered it a great honor.

sentences.zh: 高祖、太后親幸其宅，饗會百官。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu and the empress dowager personally visited his residence and feasted with the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen and the empress dowager visited his home in person and held a feast for the entire court.

sentences.zh: 祐性恭密，出入機禁二十餘年，未曾有過。

translations.literal: You's nature was respectful and discreet; for more than twenty years in entering and leaving the inner secrets he never once committed a fault.
translations.idiomatic: You was respectful and discreet; for more than twenty years in and out of the inner sanctum he never once gave offense.

sentences.zh: 由是特被恩寵，歲月賞賜，家累巨萬。

translations.literal: For this reason he was especially favored and graced; month by month he received rewards and gifts, and his household amassed wealth in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: For this he received extraordinary favor: month after month came rewards and gifts until his household held wealth counted in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 與王質等十七人俱賜金券，許以不死。

translations.literal: Together with Wang Zhi and seventeen others he was all granted gold certificates, with assurance that he would not be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: He and Wang Zhi, together with seventeen others, were granted gold certificates guaranteeing immunity from execution.

sentences.zh: 太和十年薨，時年四十九。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Taihe he died, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth year of the Taihe era, at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 高祖親臨之，詔鴻臚典護喪事。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu came in person to his side and ordered the Grand Master of Ceremonies to direct the funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen came in person and ordered the Grand Master of Ceremonies to oversee the funeral.

sentences.zh: 賜帛千匹，贈征南大將軍、司空公，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He was granted a thousand bolts of silk and posthumously made General Who Pacifies the South and Duke of Works, with posthumous name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted a thousand bolts of silk and posthumously made him General Who Pacifies the South and Duke of Works, with the posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 葬日，車駕親送出郊。

translations.literal: On the day of the burial, the imperial carriage personally escorted him out to the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the burial the emperor personally escorted the coffin out of the city.

sentences.zh: 祐養子顯明，後名慶，少歷內職。

translations.literal: You's adopted son Xianming, later named Qing, from youth held posts within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: You's adopted son Xianming, who later took the name Qing, held palace posts from an early age.

sentences.zh: 有姿貌，江陽王繼以女妻之。

translations.literal: He had good looks; Prince Jiangyang Ji gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome in bearing, he married a daughter of Prince Jiangyang Ji.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，降為隴東公，又降為侯。

translations.literal: He inherited the title, which was reduced to Duke of Longdong, and again reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title, which was first reduced to Duke of Longdong and then to marquis.

sentences.zh: 遷洛，廢替二十餘年，虛爵而已。

translations.literal: After the move to Luoyang, for more than twenty years he was dismissed and replaced, holding only a hollow title.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital moved to Luoyang, he was sidelined for more than twenty years, holding nothing but an empty title.

sentences.zh: 熙平初，為員外常侍、兼衞尉少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiping he was made Supernumerary Regular Attendant and concurrently Vice Director of the Court of Guards.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xiping era he was made Supernumerary Regular Attendant and concurrently Vice Director of the Court of Guards.

sentences.zh: 以元叉姊壻，故越次而授焉。

translations.literal: Because he was the husband of Yuan Cha's elder sister, he was therefore appointed out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was Yuan Cha's brother-in-law, he was promoted ahead of his proper turn.

sentences.zh: 神龜二年冬，靈太后為肅宗采名家女，慶女入充世婦，未幾為嬪，即叉甥也。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Shengui, Empress Dowager Ling selected daughters of eminent families for Emperor Suzong; Qing's daughter entered as heir-apparent consort attendant, and before long became a concubine—she was Yuan Cha's niece.
