translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Shengui, Empress Dowager Ling selected daughters of eminent families for Emperor Suzong. Qing's daughter entered the palace as an attendant to the heir-apparent's consort and soon became a concubine—Yuan Cha's niece.

sentences.zh: 正光三年，正少卿，尋出為將軍、高平鎮將。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengguang he was made full Vice Director, and soon after was sent out as General and Commandant of Gaoping Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhengguang he was confirmed as full Vice Director, and soon afterward was sent out as General and Commandant of Gaoping Garrison.

sentences.zh: 卒，子迥洛襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Jionglo inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Jionglo inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 抱嶷，字道德，安定石唐人，居於直谷。

translations.literal: Bao Ni, styled Daode, was a man of Shitang in Anding and lived at Zhigu.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Ni, courtesy name Daode, was from Shitang in Anding and lived at Zhigu.

sentences.zh: 自言其先姓杞，漢靈帝時杞匡為安定太守，董卓時，懼誅，由是易氏，即家焉。

translations.literal: He himself said his ancestors bore the surname Qi; in Emperor Ling of Han's time Qi Kuang was Administrator of Anding; in Dong Zhuo's time, fearing execution, for this reason they changed the surname and made that place their home.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed his ancestors had borne the surname Qi. In the reign of Emperor Ling of Han, Qi Kuang served as Administrator of Anding; during Dong Zhuo's ascendancy, fearing death, the family changed its surname and settled there.

sentences.zh: 無得而知也。

translations.literal: There is no way to know this for certain.
translations.idiomatic: None of this can be verified.

sentences.zh: 幼時，隴東人張乾王反叛，家染其逆。

translations.literal: In his youth, when Zhang Ganwang of Longdong rebelled, the family was tainted by the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth, when Zhang Ganwang of Longdong rebelled, the family was implicated in the revolt.

sentences.zh: 及乾王敗，父睹生逃逸得免，嶷獨與母沒內京都，遂為宦人。

translations.literal: When Ganwang was defeated, his father Dusheng fled and escaped; Ni alone, with his mother, was captured and sent to the inner capital, and thus became a eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: When Ganwang was defeated, his father Dusheng fled and survived, but Ni and his mother alone were captured and sent to the inner capital, where Ni became a eunuch.

sentences.zh: 小心慎密，恭以奉上，沉跡冗散，經十九年。

translations.literal: Careful and discreet, respectful in serving those above, he sank into obscure redundant posts for nineteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Careful and discreet, he served his superiors with dutiful humility and spent nineteen years in obscure, lowly posts.

sentences.zh: 後以忠謹被擢，累遷為中常侍、安西將軍、中曹侍御、尚書，賜爵安定公。

translations.literal: Later, for loyalty and prudence he was promoted, and repeatedly rose to Regular Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the West, Attendant of the Internal Directorate, Master of Writing, and was granted the title Duke of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Later his loyalty and reliability won promotion, and he rose through the ranks to Regular Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the West, Attendant of the Internal Directorate, and Master of Writing, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Anding.

sentences.zh: 自總納言，職當機近，諸所奏議，必致抗直。

translations.literal: Once he held chief counsel, his post was close to the inner secrets; in all memorials submitted he invariably spoke frankly and uprightly.
translations.idiomatic: Once at the head of state counsel with duties close to the throne, every memorial he submitted was forthright and uncompromising.

sentences.zh: 高祖、文明太后嘉之，以為殿中侍御，尚書領中曹如故，以統宿衞。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenming praised this and made him Attendant of the Palace Hall, with Master of Writing continuing to head the Internal Directorate as before, to command the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming approved and made him Attendant of the Palace Hall while keeping him as Master of Writing in charge of the Internal Directorate, putting him in command of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 俄加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Before long he was given the added title Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was also made Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 高祖、太后每出遊幸，嶷多驂乘，入則後宮導引。

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Gaozu and the empress dowager went out on tour, Ni often rode in the accompanying carriage; when inside, he guided the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Xiaowen and the empress dowager traveled, Ni often rode in the accompanying carriage; inside the palace he served as guide to the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 太后既寵之，乃徵其父睹生，拜太中大夫，賞賜衣馬。

translations.literal: Since the empress dowager favored him, she summoned his father Dusheng and appointed him Grand Master of the Palace, granting clothes and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Because the empress dowager favored him, she summoned his father Dusheng, made him Grand Master of the Palace, and rewarded him with clothes and horses.

sentences.zh: 睹生將還，見於皇信堂。

translations.literal: When Dusheng was about to return, he was received in audience at Huangxin Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Dusheng was about to leave, he was received in audience at Huangxin Hall.

sentences.zh: 高祖執手謂之曰：「老人歸途，幾日可達，好慎行路。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu took his hand and said to him: "Old man, on the return journey, how many days until you arrive? Take good care on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen took his hand and said, "Old man, on your journey home, how many days until you arrive? Take good care on the road.

sentences.zh: 」太和十二年，遷都曹，加侍中、祭酒，尚書領中曹、侍御。

translations.literal: " In the twelfth year of Taihe he was transferred to the Directorate of Masters of Writing, with added Chamberlain and Libationer, Master of Writing continuing to head the Internal Directorate and Attendant office.
translations.idiomatic: " In the twelfth year of Taihe he was transferred to the Directorate of Masters of Writing, made Chamberlain and Libationer, and continued as Master of Writing in charge of the Internal Directorate and Attendant office.

sentences.zh: [8]後降爵為侯。

translations.literal: [8] Later his title was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Later his title was reduced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 睹生卒，贈秦州刺史，諡曰靖。

translations.literal: When Dusheng died, he was posthumously granted Inspector of Qin Province, with posthumous name Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When Dusheng died, he was posthumously made Inspector of Qin Province, with the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 賜黃金八十斤、繒綵及絹八百匹，以供喪用，并別使勞慰。

translations.literal: He was granted eighty jin of gold, silk brocades and eight hundred bolts of silk for funeral expenses, and a separate envoy was sent to express condolences.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted eighty jin of gold, brocade, and eight hundred bolts of silk for the funeral, and sent a special envoy to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 加嶷大長秋卿。

translations.literal: Ni was additionally made Director of the Palace Park.
translations.idiomatic: Ni was further appointed Director of the Palace Park.

sentences.zh: 嶷老疾，請乞外祿，乃以為鎮西將軍、涇州刺史，特加右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Ni, old and ill, requested leave and external stipend; he was therefore made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jing Province, with specially added Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Old and ill, Ni asked to retire on provincial salary and was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jing Province, with the added honor of Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 將之州，高祖餞於西郊樂陽殿，以御白羽扇賜之。

translations.literal: As he was about to go to his province, Emperor Gaozu saw him off at Leyang Hall in the western suburbs and granted him the imperial white feather fan.
translations.idiomatic: As he set out for his province, Emperor Xiaowen saw him off at Leyang Hall in the western suburbs and gave him the imperial white feather fan.

sentences.zh: 十九年，被詔赴洛，以刺史從駕南征，常參侍左右。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was ordered to come to Luoyang and, as inspector, followed the imperial progress on the southern campaign, constantly attending at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was summoned to Luoyang and, as provincial inspector, joined the emperor's southern campaign, constantly in attendance at his side.

sentences.zh: 以嶷耆舊，每見勞問，數追稱嶷之正直。

translations.literal: Because Ni was an elder statesman, the emperor whenever he saw him inquired after him with words of comfort, and repeatedly praised Ni's integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Because Ni was a man of long service, the emperor repeatedly greeted him with kind words and spoke often of his integrity.

sentences.zh: 命乘馬出入行禁之間，與司徒馮誕同例。

translations.literal: He was ordered to ride a horse in entering and leaving the forbidden precincts, on the same terms as Minister of Works Feng Dan.
translations.idiomatic: He was permitted to ride horseback in and out of the forbidden precincts, on the same terms as the Minister of Works Feng Dan.

sentences.zh: 軍回還州。

translations.literal: When the army returned he went back to his province.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he went back to his province.

sentences.zh: 自以故老前宦，為政多守往法，不能遵用新制。

translations.literal: Considering himself an old-timer and a former eunuch official, in governing he mostly kept to old methods and could not follow the new institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing himself as an old hand from the eunuch service, he governed mostly by the old rules and could not adapt to the new institutions.

sentences.zh: 侮慢舊族，簡於接禮。

translations.literal: He insulted and slighted the old aristocratic families and was careless in observing ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: He insulted the old aristocratic families and was lax in observing ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 天性酷薄，雖弟姪甥壻，略無存潤。

translations.literal: By nature he was harsh and cold; even toward younger brothers, nephews, and sons-in-law he showed scarcely any kindness or generosity.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was harsh and cold; even toward brothers, nephews, and sons-in-law he showed almost no kindness.

sentences.zh: 後數年，卒於州。

translations.literal: Several years later he died in his province.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he died in office in his province.

sentences.zh: 先以從弟老壽為後，又養太師馮熙子次興。

translations.literal: Earlier he had made his younger cousin Laoshou his heir, and also adopted Cixing, a son of Grand Preceptor Feng Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier named his younger cousin Laoshou as heir and also adopted Cixing, a son of Grand Preceptor Feng Xi.

sentences.zh: 嶷死後，二人爭立。

translations.literal: After Ni died, the two men contended over succession.
translations.idiomatic: After Ni's death, the two men fought over the succession.

sentences.zh: 嶷妻張氏致訟經年，得以熙子為後。

translations.literal: Ni's wife, the Lady Zhang, pursued a lawsuit for years and succeeded in having Feng Xi's son established as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Ni's wife, Lady Zhang, sued for years and finally secured recognition of Feng Xi's son as heir.

sentences.zh: 老壽亦仍陳訴，終獲紹爵。

translations.literal: Laoshou also continued to appeal, and in the end succeeded in inheriting the title.
translations.idiomatic: Laoshou kept pressing his claim and in the end also won the right to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 次興還於本族，給奴婢三十口。

translations.literal: Cixing was returned to his original clan and was given thirty household slaves and maidservants.
translations.idiomatic: Cixing was sent back to his birth family and given thirty slaves and maidservants.

sentences.zh: 嶷前後賜賞奴婢牛馬蓋數百千，他物稱是。

translations.literal: The slaves, cattle, and horses that Ni had been granted in reward before and after numbered perhaps several tens or hundreds, and other goods were comparable.
translations.idiomatic: The slaves, cattle, and horses Ni had received in gifts over the years probably numbered in the hundreds, and his other possessions were on the same scale.

sentences.zh: 老壽凡薄，酒色肆情。

translations.literal: Laoshou was altogether base; he indulged freely in wine and women.
translations.idiomatic: Laoshou was altogether worthless and gave himself over to wine and women.

sentences.zh: 御史中尉王顯奏言：「風聞前洛州刺史陰平子石榮、積射將軍抱老壽恣蕩非軌，易室而姦，臊聲布於朝野，醜音被於行路，即攝鞫問，皆與風聞無差。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Censors Wang Xian memorialized: "It has been heard on the wind that the former Inspector of Luo Province Shiyinzi Shi Rong and the Honorary General of the Rapid Tiger Bao Laoshou indulged in unrestrained misconduct, changed wives to commit adultery, foul rumors spread through court and countryside, and vile talk filled the roads; upon immediate arrest and interrogation, all matched what was heard on the wind.
translations.idiomatic: The Inspector of Censors Wang Xian memorialized: "Word has reached me that the former Inspector of Luo Province Shiyinzi Shi Rong and the Honorary General of the Rapid Tiger Bao Laoshou have indulged in rank debauchery, swapped wives and bedmates, and that foul gossip fills the capital and the roads alike. Upon investigation, all of it proves true.

sentences.zh: 犯禮傷化，老壽等即主。

translations.literal: In violating ritual and harming customs, Laoshou and the others are the principals.
translations.idiomatic: Laoshou and the others are the chief offenders against ritual and public decency.

sentences.zh: 謹案：石榮籍貫兵伍，地隔宦流，處世無入朝之期，在生絕冠冕之望。

translations.literal: Respectfully submitted: Shi Rong's register originates in the military ranks; his region is separated from the eunuch stream; in the world he had no prospect of entering court; in life he had no hope of wearing official caps.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully submit: Shi Rong came from the military ranks, far removed from the eunuch class; he could never have expected to enter court, nor in ordinary life could he have hoped for official rank.

sentences.zh: 遭時之運，逢非次之擢，以犬馬延慈，簪履恩念，自微至貴，位階方岳。

translations.literal: Meeting the fortune of the times, he received promotion beyond his station; by extending canine and equine kindness he was graced, and in hairpin and shoes there was gracious remembrance; from humble to noble, his rank reached that of a regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: By the luck of the times he was raised far above his station, advancing from humble service to the highest favor, from insignificance to a rank equal to a provincial governor.

sentences.zh: 不能懷恩感德，上酬天施，迺咎彰遐邇，嚮穢京墟。

translations.literal: He could not harbor gratitude and respond to virtue, to requite heaven's bounty on high; instead guilt was manifest near and far, and filth spread through the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He failed to repay that extraordinary grace and instead brought shame on himself near and far, defiling the capital itself.

sentences.zh: 老壽種類無聞，氏姓莫紀，丐乞刑餘之家，覆養閹人之室。

translations.literal: Laoshou's kind and lineage are unknown, his clan and surname unrecorded; he begged his way into a family punished by castration and was reared in a eunuch's household.
translations.idiomatic: Laoshou's origins are unknown and his clan unrecorded; he was taken in from a family condemned to castration and raised in a eunuch household.

sentences.zh: 蒙國殊澤，預班爵序，正宜治家假內，

translations.literal: Receiving the state's extraordinary grace, admitted to the ranks of nobility, he ought rightly to manage the household and keep within the inner bounds,
translations.idiomatic: Granted extraordinary favor by the state and enrolled among the nobility, he ought to have managed his household and kept within proper bounds,

translations.literal: 〈doubtful text〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈text corrupt here〉

sentences.zh: 教誡閨庭。

translations.literal: and teach and admonish within the women's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: and set an example of discipline within the family.

sentences.zh: 方恣其淫姦，換妻易妾。

translations.literal: Instead he indulged his lewd adultery, swapping wives and changing concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he gave himself to lewd adultery, swapping wives and concubines at will.

sentences.zh: 榮前在洛州，遠迎老壽妻常氏，兵人千里，疲於道路。

translations.literal: When Rong was previously in Luo Province, he sent men a thousand li to bring Laoshou's wife, the Lady Chang; soldiers were worn out on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong was Inspector of Luo Province, he sent men a thousand li to fetch Laoshou's wife, Lady Chang, wearing out soldiers on the road.

sentences.zh: 老壽同敝笱之在梁，若其原

translations.literal: Laoshou was like a worn fish-trap at the beam; as for his origin
translations.idiomatic: Laoshou was like a worn fish-trap on the rafter; as for the lineage

translations.literal: 〈doubtful text〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈text corrupt here〉

sentences.zh: 之無別，男女三人，莫知誰子。

translations.literal: there was no distinction; three children, male and female, and no one knew whose they were.
translations.idiomatic: there was no telling them apart—three children, and no one knew who the fathers were.

sentences.zh: 人理所未聞，鳥獸之不若。

translations.literal: Such a thing is unheard of in human reason and is beneath even birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing like this has ever been heard among men; even birds and beasts do not sink so low.

sentences.zh: 請以見事，免官付廷尉理罪，鴻臚削爵。

translations.literal: I request that on the basis of what has been established, they be removed from office and handed to the Court of Judicial Review for punishment, and that the Grand Master of Ceremonies strip their titles.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that, on the basis of the facts established, they be dismissed from office and handed over to the Court of Judicial Review for punishment, and that the Grand Master of Ceremonies strip them of their titles.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 老壽妻常氏，萬敵弟女也。

translations.literal: Laoshou's wife, Lady Chang, was the daughter of Wandi's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Laoshou's wife, Lady Chang, was the daughter of Wandi's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 老壽死後，收紀家業，稍復其舊，奴婢尚六七百人。

translations.literal: After Laoshou died, the family estate was gathered and recorded; it was gradually restored to its former state, and there were still six or seven hundred male and female slaves.
translations.idiomatic: After Laoshou's death, the family estate was gathered and settled; it was gradually restored, and six or seven hundred bond servants still remained.

sentences.zh: 三女並嬪貴室。

translations.literal: Three daughters all became concubines in the noble quarters.
translations.idiomatic: All three daughters became concubines in the imperial inner apartments.

sentences.zh: 為老壽祖父皆造碑銘，自洛就鄉而建之。

translations.literal: For all of Laoshou's grandfathers he had stele inscriptions made, leaving Luoyang to return to the homeland to erect them.
translations.idiomatic: He had commemorative steles made for all of Laoshou's grandfathers, then left Luoyang for the countryside to set them up.

sentences.zh: 西方云，直谷出二貴人。

translations.literal: In the west they say that from Zhigu came two eminent persons.
translations.idiomatic: People in the west say that two great men came from Zhigu.

sentences.zh: 石榮者，從主書稍進為州。

translations.literal: Shi Rong rose from Clerk Attached to the Director to become, by gradual promotion, a provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Rong had risen from a clerk attached to the Director to a provincial governorship.

sentences.zh: 自被劾後，遂便廢頓。

translations.literal: From the time he was impeached, he then fell into ruin and stagnation.
translations.idiomatic: After he was impeached, he fell into complete decline.

sentences.zh: 子長宣，武定中，南兗州刺史，與侯景反，伏法。

translations.literal: His son Changxuan, in the Wuding era, was Inspector of Southern Yan Province; he joined Hou Jing's rebellion and was executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changxuan served as Inspector of Southern Yan Province in the Wuding era; he joined Hou Jing's rebellion and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 王遇，字慶時，本名他惡，馮翊李潤鎮羌也。

translations.literal: Wang Yu, styled Qingshi, original name Ta'e, was from Zhenqiang in Lirun, Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu, styled Qingshi, whose original name was Ta'e, came from Zhenqiang in Lirun, Fufeng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 與雷、党、不蒙俱為羌中強族。

translations.literal: Together with Lei, Dang, and Bumeng, they were all powerful clans among the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: He belonged, with the Lei, Dang, and Bumeng clans, to the great Qiang families of the region.

sentences.zh: [9]自云其先姓王，後改氏鉗耳，世宗時復改為王焉。

translations.literal: [9]He said that his ancestors originally bore the surname Wang, later changed their clan name to Qian'er, and in Emperor Shizong's time changed back to Wang.
translations.idiomatic: [9]He claimed that his ancestors had originally borne the surname Wang, later took the clan name Qian'er, and in the reign of Emperor Xuanwu changed back to Wang.

sentences.zh: 自晉世已來，恒為渠長。

translations.literal: From the Jin era onward, they were constantly headmen of the military colony.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jin era, his family had regularly served as headmen of the military colony.

sentences.zh: 父守貴，為郡功曹，卒。

translations.literal: His father Shougui served as Merit Officer of the commandery and died.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shougui was a Merit Officer of the commandery and died in office.

sentences.zh: 遇既貴，追贈安西將軍、秦州刺史、澄城公。

translations.literal: Once Yu became honored, he was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the West, Inspector of Qin Province, and Duke of Chengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Yu rose to prominence, his father was posthumously enfeoffed as General Who Pacifies the West, Inspector of Qin Province, and Duke of Chengcheng.

sentences.zh: 遇坐事腐刑，為中散，遷內行令、中曹給事中，加員外散騎常侍、右將軍，賜爵富平子。

translations.literal: Yu, because of an offense, suffered castration; he served as Palace Attendant, was promoted to Director of Internal Service and Attendant Within of the Internal Directorate, was additionally made Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Disheveled Riders and General of the Right, and was granted the title Marquis of Fuping.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was sentenced to castration for an offense, then served as a palace attendant; he rose to Director of Internal Service and Attendant Within in the Internal Directorate, was also made Supernumerary Regular Attendant and General of the Right, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fuping.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍、安西將軍，進爵宕昌公。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Disheveled Riders and General Who Pacifies the West, and advanced in rank to Duke of Dangchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Regular Attendant and General Who Pacifies the West, and raised to Duke of Dangchang.

sentences.zh: 拜尚書，轉吏部尚書，仍常侍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Master of Writing, transferred to Master of Writing of the Personnel Bureau, and remained Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to the Masters of Writing, then transferred to head the Personnel Bureau while retaining his post as Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 例降為侯。

translations.literal: By precedent his rank was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: By established rule, his title was reduced from duke to marquis.

sentences.zh: 出為安西將軍、華州刺史，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was sent out as General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Hua Province, with the additional title Regular Attendant of the Disheveled Riders.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Hua Province, with the additional rank of Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 幽后之前廢也，遇頗言其過。

translations.literal: Before Empress You was deposed, Yu spoke at length of her faults.
translations.idiomatic: Before Empress You was deposed, Yu had spoken at length about her faults.

sentences.zh: 及後進幸，高祖對李沖等申后無咎，而稱遇謗議之罪。

translations.literal: When afterward she was again favored, Emperor Gaozu declared to Li Chong and the others that the empress was without guilt, and charged Yu with the crime of slander and criticism.
translations.idiomatic: When she later regained the emperor's favor, Emperor Xiaowen told Li Chong and the others that the empress was innocent and charged Yu with slander.

sentences.zh: 沖言：「果爾，遇合死也。

translations.literal: Chong said, "If it is truly so, Yu deserves death.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong said, "If that is so, Yu deserves death.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「遇舊人，未忍盡之，當止黜廢耳。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gaozu said, "Yu is an old associate; I cannot bear to go all the way—I shall only dismiss and disgrace him.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xiaowen said, "Yu is an old associate, and I cannot bring myself to destroy him outright—dismissal and disgrace will be enough.

sentences.zh: 」遂遣御史馳驛免遇官，奪其爵，收衣冠，以民還私第。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he dispatched an imperial censor by post relay to remove Yu from office, strip his title, confiscate his official robes and cap, and send him home as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: " He then sent an imperial censor posthaste to dismiss Yu from office, strip him of his title, take back his robes of rank, and send him home as a private citizen.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，兼將作大匠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign, he additionally served as Grand Master of Construction.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign, he additionally served as Grand Master of Construction.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜光祿大夫，復奪爵。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and his title was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and the title that had been taken from him was restored.

translations.literal: [10] In Bei Shi 92, Wang Yu's biography reads 'restored his former title' (fu jiu jue), which is clearer. Here the meaning is that the forfeited title was restored, though the wording could easily be misunderstood as a second forfeiture.
translations.idiomatic: [10] The History of the Northern Dynasties reads 'restored his former title,' which is clearer: the passage means his confiscated rank was given back, not that it was stripped away a second time.

sentences.zh: 廢后馮氏之為尼也，公私罕相供恤。

translations.literal: When the deposed empress, Lady Feng, became a nun, public and private persons rarely came to her aid or comfort.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed Empress Feng became a nun, few in court or in private life offered her support or sympathy.

sentences.zh: 遇自以常更奉接，往來祗謁，不替舊敬，衣食雜物，每有薦奉。

translations.literal: Yu, considering that he had long served her in attendance, continued to come and go in reverent visitation without diminishing his old respect; for food, clothing, and miscellaneous goods he always made offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, who had long attended her in service, continued to visit her with the same deference as before, and regularly sent her food, clothing, and other necessities.

sentences.zh: 后皆受而不讓。

translations.literal: The empress always accepted them and did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: The empress accepted everything and never refused.

sentences.zh: 又至其館，遇夫妻迎送謁伏，侍立執臣妾之禮。

translations.literal: When he came again to her lodging, Yu and his wife welcomed and escorted her, prostrating themselves in obeisance, standing in attendance and performing the rites of subject and concubine.
translations.idiomatic: When he visited her residence, Yu and his wife greeted and escorted her with full prostration, standing at attention and behaving like subjects before their mistress.

sentences.zh: 遇性巧，強於部分。

translations.literal: Yu was clever by nature and strong in planning and allocation.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was ingenious by nature and especially skilled at organizing work.

sentences.zh: 北都方山靈泉道俗居宇及文明太后陵廟，洛京東郊馬射壇殿，修廣文昭太后墓園，太極殿及東西兩堂、內外諸門制度，皆遇監作。

translations.literal: The dwellings of monks and laymen at Lingquan on Fangshan in the northern capital and the tomb-shrine of Empress Dowager Wenming; the archery pavilion and hall in the eastern suburbs of Luoyang; the expansion of the tomb park of Empress Wen Zhao; and the regulations for the Hall of Grand Ultimate and the eastern and western halls, and all the inner and outer gates—these Yu supervised in construction.
translations.idiomatic: Yu supervised construction of the dwellings of monks and laymen at Lingquan on Fangshan in the northern capital and the shrine of Empress Dowager Wenming; the archery pavilion in Luoyang's eastern suburbs; the expansion of Empress Wen Zhao's tomb park; and the design of the Hall of Grand Ultimate, its eastern and western halls, and all the inner and outer palace gates.

sentences.zh: 雖年在耆老，朝夕不倦，跨鞍驅馳，與少壯者均其勞逸。

translations.literal: Although advanced in years, morning and evening he did not tire; mounting the saddle and driving on horseback, he shared equally in toil and rest with the young and strong.
translations.idiomatic: Though he was already elderly, he never flagged from dawn to dusk: he rode horseback and shared the labor equally with men half his age.

sentences.zh: 又長於人事，留意酒食之間，每逢僚舊，具設餚果，觴膳精豐。

translations.literal: He was also skilled in human relations, attentive in the intervals of feasting and drinking; whenever he met colleagues and old associates, he fully laid out delicacies and fruits, and the cups and viands were refined and abundant.
translations.idiomatic: He was also skilled at managing people and took care over hospitality: whenever old colleagues visited, he spread out fine delicacies and wines in generous abundance.

sentences.zh: 然競於榮利，趨求勢門。

translations.literal: Yet he competed for glory and profit and pressed toward powerful families.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was greedy for rank and profit and ever courting the powerful.

sentences.zh: 趙脩之寵也，遇往還宗承，受敕為之監作第宅，增於本旨，笞擊作人，莫不嗟怒。

translations.literal: When Zhao Xiu was favored, Yu went back and forth paying him respect and homage; receiving an edict to supervise construction of his residence, he exceeded the original mandate and flogged the laborers, and none did not sigh in anger.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Xiu was in favor, Yu paid him constant court; ordered to supervise construction of his mansion, he went beyond what had been authorized and beat the workmen until all who saw it groaned in outrage.

sentences.zh: 卒于官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 初，遇之疾也，太傅、北海王與太妃俱往臨問，視其危惙，為之泣下。

translations.literal: At first, when Yu fell ill, the Grand Tutor, Prince of Beihai, and the princess consort both went to visit him at his bedside; seeing how perilously weak he was, they wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu first fell ill, the Grand Tutor, Prince of Beihai, and his consort both came to his bedside; seeing how close to death he was, they wept.

sentences.zh: 其善奉諸貴，致相悲悼如此。

translations.literal: Such was the mutual grief and mourning to which his skill at serving the nobles gave rise.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the mourning he earned by his attentiveness to the great.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、鎮西將軍、雍州刺史，侯如故。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted bearer of the staff of authority, General Who Guards the West, and Inspector of Yong Province; his marquisate remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Bearer of the Staff, General Who Guards the West, and Inspector of Yong Province, with his marquisate unchanged.

sentences.zh: 始遇與抱嶷並為文明太后所寵，前後賜以奴婢數百人，馬牛羊他物稱是，二人俱號富室。

translations.literal: From the first Yu and Bao Ni were both favored by Empress Dowager Wenming; before and after they were granted several hundred male and female slaves, horses, cattle, sheep, and other goods in like measure, and the two were both styled wealthy households.
translations.idiomatic: From the beginning Wang Yu and Bao Ni were both favorites of Empress Dowager Wenming; she lavished on them several hundred bond servants, horses, cattle, sheep, and goods in proportion, and both were reckoned fabulously rich.

sentences.zh: 遇養弟子厲，本郡太守。

translations.literal: Yu raised his younger brother's son Li as his heir; he was Grand Administrator of the native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yu adopted his younger brother's son Li, who served as Grand Administrator of their home commandery.

sentences.zh: 稍遷至右軍將軍，襲爵宕昌侯。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to General of the Right Army and inherited the title Marquis of Dangchang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose gradually to General of the Right Army and inherited the title Marquis of Dangchang.

sentences.zh: 產業有過于遇時。

translations.literal: His estate and possessions surpassed those of Yu in his day.
translations.idiomatic: His wealth even exceeded what Yu had possessed in his prime.

sentences.zh: 苻承祖，略陽氐人也。

translations.literal: Fu Chengzu was a man of the Di of Lueyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chengzu was a Di from Lueyang.

sentences.zh: 因事為閹人，為文明太后所寵，自御厩令遷中部給事中、散騎常侍、輔國將軍，賜爵略陽侯，兼典選部事，中部如故。

translations.literal: Because of an affair he became a eunuch; favored by Empress Dowager Wenming, he rose from Director of the Imperial Stud to Attendant Within of the Central Directorate, Regular Attendant of the Disheveled Riders, and General Who Assists the State, was granted the title Marquis of Lueyang, and additionally oversaw the Personnel Bureau, while his post in the Central Directorate remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Reduced to a eunuch for an offense, he won the favor of Empress Dowager Wenming; he rose from Director of the Imperial Stud to Attendant Within in the Central Directorate, Regular Attendant, and General Who Assists the State, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Lueyang, and was also put in charge of the Personnel Bureau while retaining his Central Directorate post.

sentences.zh: 轉吏部尚書，仍領中部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Master of Writing of the Personnel Bureau, still heading the Central Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to head the Personnel Bureau while continuing to lead the Central Directorate.

sentences.zh: 高祖為造甲第，數臨幸之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu built for him a mansion of the first rank and repeatedly visited it in person.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen built him a grand mansion and visited it repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 進爵略陽公，安南將軍，加侍中，知都曹事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Duke of Lueyang and General Who Pacifies the South, was additionally made Palace Attendant, and given charge of the Directorate of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to Duke of Lueyang and General Who Pacifies the South, made Palace Attendant, and put in charge of the Directorate of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 初太后以承祖居腹心之任，許以不死之詔。

translations.literal: At first the empress dowager, because Chengzu held a post close to her heart, granted him an edict promising he would not be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Because Chengzu held one of her most trusted posts, the empress dowager had granted him an edict guaranteeing he would not be executed.

sentences.zh: 後承祖坐贓應死，高祖原之，削職禁錮在家，授悖義將軍、佞濁子，月餘遂死。

translations.literal: Later Chengzu, because of bribery, deserved death; Emperor Gaozu pardoned him, stripped him of office and confined him at home, granted him the title General of Perverse Loyalty and Viscount of Sycophantic Filth, and within little more than a month he died.
translations.idiomatic: Later Chengzu was convicted of bribery and faced execution; Emperor Xiaowen spared his life, stripped him of office, and confined him at home under the mocking titles General of Perverse Loyalty and Viscount of Sycophantic Filth; he died a little over a month later.

sentences.zh: 王質，字紹奴，高陽易人也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi, styled Shaonu, was a man of Yi in Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi, styled Shaonu, came from Yi in Gaoyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 其家坐事，幼下蠶室。

translations.literal: His family suffered punishment for an offense, and while still young he entered the silkworm chamber.
translations.idiomatic: His family was punished for an offense, and he was castrated while still a boy.

sentences.zh: 頗解書學，為中曹吏、內典監。

translations.literal: He was fairly well versed in writing and learning; he served as Clerk of the Internal Directorate and Director of the Internal Canon.
translations.idiomatic: Well educated for his rank, he served as a clerk in the Internal Directorate and as Director of the Internal Canon.

sentences.zh: 稍遷祕書中散，加寧朔將軍，賜爵永昌子，領監御。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Palace Attendant of the Secretariat, additionally made General Who Pacifies the North, granted the title Viscount of Yongchang, and put in charge of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Palace Attendant in the Secretariat, was also made General Who Pacifies the North, enfeoffed as Viscount of Yongchang, and put in charge of the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 遷為侍御給事，又領選部、監御二曹事，復特加前將軍，進爵魏昌侯。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Service Within, again headed the two bureaus of the Personnel Department and the Imperial Guard, was specially additionally made General of the Vanguard, and advanced to Marquis of Weichang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant Service Within, again put in charge of both the Personnel Bureau and the Imperial Guard, additionally made General of the Vanguard, and raised to Marquis of Weichang.

sentences.zh: 轉選部尚書，加員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Master of Writing of the Selection Bureau and additionally made Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Disheveled Riders.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to head the Selection Bureau and was also made Supernumerary Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 出為鎮遠將軍、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as General Who Guards the Distance and Inspector of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as General Who Guards the Distance and Inspector of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 質在州十年，風化粗行，察姦糾慝，究其情狀，民庶畏服之。

translations.literal: Zhi spent ten years in the province; rough customs and moral transformation were put into practice, he investigated wickedness and exposed evil, pursued matters to their full circumstances, and the common people feared and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi governed the province for ten years; he gradually improved local customs, investigated crime, pursued cases to the bottom, and the people feared and obeyed him.

sentences.zh: 而刑政刻峻，多所笞戮，號為威酷。

translations.literal: Yet his punishments and administration were harsh and severe; he frequently flogged and executed, and was styled formidable and cruel.
translations.idiomatic: But his justice was harsh, and he flogged and killed so often that he was known as a merciless enforcer.

sentences.zh: 高祖頗念其忠勤宿舊，每行留大故，馮司徒亡，廢馮后，陸叡、穆泰等事，皆賜質以璽書，手筆莫不委至，同之戚貴。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu remembered his long-standing loyalty and diligence; whenever there was a major matter requiring the emperor's stay or departure, such as Minister Feng's death, the deposition of Empress Feng, and the cases of Lu Rui and Mu Tai, he always bestowed on Zhi sealed edicts, and in his own hand nothing was left uncommunicated, treating him the same as close kinsmen of honor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen valued his long loyalty; on every major occasion when the emperor remained at court or departed—Minister Feng's death, the deposition of Empress Feng, the Lu Rui and Mu Tai affair—he bestowed sealed edicts on Zhi, writing to him in his own hand with the same intimacy he showed his most honored kin.

sentences.zh: 質皆寶掌以為榮。

translations.literal: Zhi treasured and kept them all as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi treasured them all as marks of honor.

sentences.zh: 入為大長秋卿，未幾而卒。

translations.literal: He entered court as Grand Master of the Long Autumn and before long died.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Grand Master of the Long Autumn and died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 李堅，字次壽，高陽易人也。

translations.literal: Li Jian, styled Cishou, was a man of Yi in Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jian, styled Cishou, came from Yi in Gaoyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 高宗初，因事為閹人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozong's reign, because of an affair he became a eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Wencheng's reign, he was made a eunuch because of an offense.

sentences.zh: 文明太后臨朝，稍遷至中給事中，賜爵魏昌伯。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Wenming held court, he was gradually promoted to Attendant Within of the Central Directorate and granted the title Baron of Weichang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Dowager Wenming's regency he rose to Attendant Within in the Central Directorate and was enfeoffed as Baron of Weichang.

sentences.zh: 小心謹慎，常在左右，雖不及王遇、王質等，而亦見任用。

translations.literal: Careful and cautious, he was constantly at the side; although he did not equal Wang Yu, Wang Zhi, and the others, he too was employed.
translations.idiomatic: Careful and unobtrusive, he stayed constantly at hand; though he never ranked with Wang Yu and Wang Zhi, he too was given posts.

sentences.zh: 高祖遷洛，轉被委授，為太僕卿，檢課牧產，多有滋息。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu moved the capital to Luoyang, he was increasingly entrusted and appointed Grand Master of Equine Affairs; in inspecting and auditing pasture holdings there was much increase and growth.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang, he was given greater responsibility as Grand Master of Equine Affairs; under his oversight the imperial herds increased substantially.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，出為安東將軍、瀛州刺史，本州之榮，同於王質。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign, he was sent out as General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Ying Province; the honor of the native province was the same as for Wang Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign, he was sent out as General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Ying Province—the same honor in his home province that Wang Zhi had received.

sentences.zh: 所在受納，家產巨萬。

translations.literal: Wherever he was, he accepted gifts; his household estate reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he accepted bribes, and his household wealth ran to millions.

sentences.zh: 值京兆王愉反於冀州，堅勒眾征愉，為愉所破。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jingzhao Yu rebelled in Ji Province, Jian mustered troops to campaign against Yu and was defeated by Yu.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yu of Jingzhao rebelled in Ji Province, Jian raised troops against him and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 代還，遇風疾，拜光祿大夫，數年卒。

translations.literal: He returned to the capital, fell ill with wind disease, was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and died several years later.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to the capital he was stricken with paralysis, was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and died several years later.

sentences.zh: 贈撫軍將軍、相州刺史，賵帛五百匹。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Xiang Province; five hundred bolts of silk were sent as funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Xiang Province, and five hundred bolts of silk were granted for his funeral.

sentences.zh: 以弟子曇景為後，襲爵魏昌伯，為羽林監、直後。

translations.literal: His younger brother's son Tanjing was made his heir; he inherited the title Baron of Weichang and served as Commandant of the Feathered Forest Guard and Attendant in Direct Service.
translations.idiomatic: He made his nephew Tanjing his heir; Tanjing inherited the title Baron of Weichang and served as Commandant of the Feathered Forest Guard and Attendant in Direct Service.

sentences.zh: 秦松，不知其所由。

translations.literal: Qin Song—his origins are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Song's origins are unknown.

sentences.zh: 太和末，為中尹，遷長秋卿，賜爵高都子。

translations.literal: At the end of the Taihe era he served as Director of the Central Directorate, was transferred to Master of the Long Autumn, and granted the title Viscount of Gaodu.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Taihe era he became Director of the Central Directorate, was promoted to Master of the Long Autumn, and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Gaodu.

sentences.zh: 有罪免。

translations.literal: For an offense he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 世宗復其爵，起為光祿大夫，領中常侍。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong restored his title and recalled him as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, heading the Regular Attendant Within.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu restored his title and recalled him as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the added post of Regular Attendant Within.

sentences.zh: 遷平北將軍，領長秋卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the North and continued to head the Long Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North while continuing as Master of the Long Autumn.

sentences.zh: 出為散騎常侍、安北將軍、并州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Regular Attendant of the Disheveled Riders, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈大將軍、肆州刺史，諡曰定。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted Grand General and Inspector of Si Province; posthumous name Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand General and Inspector of Si Province, with the posthumous name Ding.

sentences.zh: 白整者，亦因事腐刑。

translations.literal: Bai Zheng, likewise because of an affair, suffered castration.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Zheng, too, was sentenced to castration for an offense.

sentences.zh: 少掌宮掖碎職，以恭敏著稱，稍遷至中常侍。

translations.literal: In youth he held minor posts in the palace women's quarters; known for respectful diligence, he was gradually promoted to Regular Attendant Within.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he held minor posts in the inner palace; known for reverent diligence, he rose gradually to Regular Attendant Within.

sentences.zh: 太和末，為長秋卿，賜爵雲陽男。

translations.literal: At the end of the Taihe era he served as Master of the Long Autumn and was granted the title Baron of Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Taihe era he became Master of the Long Autumn and was enfeoffed as Baron of Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 世宗封其妻王氏為□□縣君。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong enfeoffed his wife, Lady Wang, as Lady of □□ County.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu enfeoffed his wife, Lady Wang, as Lady of □□ County.

sentences.zh: [11]卒，贈平北將軍、并州刺史。

translations.literal: [11]He died; posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: [11]He died and was posthumously enfeoffed as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 劉騰，字青龍，本平原城民，徙屬南兗州之譙郡。

translations.literal: Liu Teng, styled Qinglong, was originally a commoner of Pingyuan City and was relocated to belong to Qiao Commandery in Southern Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Teng, styled Qinglong, was originally a commoner of Pingyuan and was resettled in Qiao Commandery, Southern Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 幼時坐事受刑，補小黃門，轉中黃門。

translations.literal: While still young, because of an offense he suffered punishment; he was appointed Junior Yellow Gate Attendant and transferred to Central Yellow Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Punished for an offense while still a boy, he entered service as a Junior Yellow Gate Attendant and was transferred to Central Yellow Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 高祖之在懸瓠，騰使詣行所。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu was at Xuanhu, Teng was sent to go to the place where the emperor was traveling.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen was at Xuanhu, Teng was dispatched to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: [12]高祖問其中事，騰具言幽后私隱，與陳留公主所告符協，由是進冗從僕射，仍中黃門。

translations.literal: [12]Emperor Gaozu asked about affairs within the palace; Teng fully related the private misconduct of Empress You, which matched what the Princess of Chenliu had reported, and on this account he was promoted to Supernumerary Vice Director of Attendants and remained Central Yellow Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: [12]Emperor Xiaowen questioned him about affairs inside the palace; Teng set out in full Empress You's secret misconduct, which agreed with what the Princess of Chenliu had reported, and for this he was promoted to Supernumerary Vice Director while retaining his post as Central Yellow Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 後與茹皓使徐兗，采召民女。

translations.literal: Later, together with Ru Hao, he was sent to Xu and Yan to collect and summon common women.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was sent with Ru Hao to Xu and Yan Provinces to gather commoner girls for the palace.

sentences.zh: 及還，遷中給事，稍遷中尹、中常侍，特加龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: When they returned, he was transferred to Attendant Within of the Central Directorate, was gradually promoted to Director of the Central Directorate and Regular Attendant Within, and was specially additionally made General of the Flying Dragon.
translations.idiomatic: On their return he was promoted to Attendant Within in the Central Directorate, then gradually to Director of the Central Directorate and Regular Attendant Within, with the additional rank of General of the Flying Dragon.

sentences.zh: 後為大長秋卿、金紫光祿大夫、太府卿。

translations.literal: Later he served as Grand Master of the Long Autumn, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Grand Master of the Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Grand Master of the Long Autumn, as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and as Grand Master of the Treasury.

sentences.zh: 肅宗踐極之始，以騰預在宮衞，封開國子，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning when Emperor Suzong ascended the throne, because Teng had participated in palace guard duty, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of a State-Founding Fief with three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaoming first took the throne, Teng was enfeoffed as Viscount of a state-founding fief with three hundred households for his service in the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 是年，靈太后臨朝，以與于忠保護之勳，除崇訓太僕，加中侍中，改封長樂縣開國公，食邑一千五百戶。

translations.literal: That year Empress Dowager Ling held court; because of the merit of protecting her together with Yu Zhong, he was appointed Grand Master of the Chongxun Palace Stud, additionally made Attendant Within, changed in enfeoffment to Duke of a State-Founding Fief of Chang Le County with one thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, with Empress Dowager Ling regent, he was made Grand Master of the Chongxun Palace Stud and Attendant Within for his part with Yu Zhong in protecting her, and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Chang Le with a fief of one thousand five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 拜其妻時為鉅鹿郡君，每引入內，受賞賚亞於諸主外戚。

translations.literal: His wife Shi was enfeoffed as Lady of Julu Commandery; each time she was brought into the inner palace, the rewards and gifts she received were second only to those of princesses and maternal relatives of the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Shi was enfeoffed as Lady of Julu Commandery; whenever she was summoned within the palace, the gifts she received ranked just below those given to princesses and the empress's kin.

sentences.zh: 所養二子，為郡守、尚書郎。

translations.literal: The two sons he had raised served as commandery grand administrators and Masters of Writing Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The two sons he had adopted served as commandery governors and secretariat officers.

sentences.zh: 騰曾疾篤，靈太后慮或不救，遷衞將軍、儀同三司，餘官仍舊。

translations.literal: When Teng once fell gravely ill, Empress Dowager Ling feared he might not recover; he was transferred to General of the Guard and received the Three Premiers as equals in honor, while his other offices remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Teng once fell gravely ill, Empress Dowager Ling, fearing he might not survive, promoted him to General of the Guard with the honorific rank equal to the Three Excellencies, while his other posts remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 後疾瘳。

translations.literal: Afterward his illness recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He later recovered from his illness.

sentences.zh: 騰之拜命，肅宗當為臨軒，會其日大風寒甚而罷，乃遣使持節授之。

translations.literal: For Teng's appointment to office, Emperor Suzong was to preside at the imperial court; but on that day the wind was bitterly cold and the ceremony was canceled, whereupon an envoy bearing the staff of authority was dispatched to invest him.
translations.idiomatic: When Teng was to receive his appointment, Emperor Xiaoming was to preside at court, but a bitter gale that day forced the ceremony to be canceled; an envoy bearing the imperial staff was sent instead to invest him with the rank.

sentences.zh: 騰幼充宮役，手不解書，裁知署名而已。

translations.literal: Teng from youth filled palace service; his hand did not understand writing—he could only sign his name, and that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Teng had served in the palace since boyhood and could barely write; he knew only how to sign his name.

sentences.zh: 姦謀有餘，善射人意。

translations.literal: He had more than enough in cunning plots and was skilled at hitting the mark in others' intentions.
translations.idiomatic: He was surpassingly cunning and uncannily adept at reading what others wanted to hear.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，特蒙進寵，多所干託，內外碎密，栖栖不倦。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling held court, he was specially favored with advancement; he made many entreaties and commissions, in inner and outer matters great and small, restless and never weary.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Dowager Ling's regency he won exceptional favor; he pressed ceaseless requests and commissions, great and small, inside the palace and out, never resting.

sentences.zh: 洛北永橋，太上公、太上君及城東三寺，皆主修營。

translations.literal: The Eternal Bridge north of Luoyang, the Grand Superior Duke and Grand Superior Lady, and the three monasteries east of the city—all these he chiefly supervised in construction.
translations.idiomatic: He personally oversaw construction of the Eternal Bridge north of Luoyang, the halls of the Grand Superior Duke and Grand Superior Lady, and three monasteries east of the city.

sentences.zh: 吏部嘗望騰意，奏其弟為郡帶戍，人資乖越，清河王懌抑而不與。

translations.literal: The Personnel Bureau once sought to please Teng's wishes and memorialized that his younger brother be given a commandery with frontier garrison duty; the man's qualifications were far beyond his station, and Prince of Qinghe Yi blocked the appointment and did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: The Personnel Bureau once tried to curry favor with Teng by recommending his younger brother for a commandery post with frontier garrison duty—a rank far above the man's merits. Prince Yi of Qinghe blocked the appointment.

sentences.zh: 騰以為恨，遂與領軍元叉害懌。

translations.literal: Teng took this as a grievance and thereupon, together with the Commandant-in-Chief Yuan Cha, killed Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Teng nursed a grudge and, together with the Commandant-in-Chief Yuan Cha, had Yi killed.

sentences.zh: 廢靈太后於宣光殿，宮門晝夜長閉，內外斷絕。

translations.literal: They deposed Empress Dowager Ling in the Hall of Xuan Radiance; the palace gates were kept shut day and night, and inner and outer were cut off from one another.
translations.idiomatic: They confined Empress Dowager Ling in the Hall of Xuan Radiance; the palace gates were kept shut day and night, cutting her off from the court and the world beyond.

sentences.zh: 騰自執管鑰，肅宗亦不得見，裁聽傳食而已。

translations.literal: Teng himself kept the keys; even Emperor Suzong could not see her—he was permitted only to have food passed in.
translations.idiomatic: Teng kept the keys himself; even Emperor Xiaoming could not see her and was allowed only to send food in.

sentences.zh: 太后服膳俱廢，不免飢寒。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's clothing and food were both abandoned; she could not escape hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Proper meals and clothing for the empress dowager were cut off, and she went hungry and cold.

sentences.zh: 又使中常侍賈粲假言侍肅宗書，密令防察。

translations.literal: They also had Regular Attendant Within Jia Can falsely say that he waited on Emperor Suzong's written orders, secretly instructing him to watch and guard.
translations.idiomatic: They also sent Regular Attendant Within Jia Can, under the pretense of attending to Emperor Xiaoming's orders, to keep her under secret surveillance.

sentences.zh: 叉以騰為司空公，表裏擅權，共相樹置。

translations.literal: Cha made Teng Duke of Works; inwardly and outwardly they monopolized power and mutually established one another.
translations.idiomatic: Cha made Teng Duke of Works; together they wielded power inside and out, propping each other up in office.

sentences.zh: 叉為外禦，騰為內防，迭直禁闥，共裁刑賞。

translations.literal: Cha served as outer defense, Teng as inner defense; they took turns on duty at the forbidden gates and jointly decided punishments and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Cha guarded the outer palace, Teng the inner; they alternated at the forbidden gates and jointly decided who would live or die, who would rise or fall.

sentences.zh: 騰遂與崔光同受詔乘步挽出入殿門。

translations.literal: Teng then received an edict together with Cui Guang to ride in a hand-drawn carriage in and out of the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: Teng and Cui Guang were then granted the privilege of riding in hand-drawn carriages through the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 四年之中，生殺之威，決於叉、騰之手。

translations.literal: Within four years, the power of life and death rested in the hands of Cha and Teng.
translations.idiomatic: For four years the power of life and death rested in the hands of Cha and Teng.

sentences.zh: 八坐、九卿，旦造騰宅，參其顏色，然後方赴省府，亦有歷日不能見者。

translations.literal: The Eight Seat-holders and Nine Ministers each morning went to Teng's residence to read his countenance, and only afterward proceeded to their ministries; some went for days without being received.
translations.idiomatic: The Eight Excellencies and Nine Ministers called each morning at Teng's house to read his mood before going to their offices; some waited days without gaining an audience.

sentences.zh: 公私屬請，唯在財貨。

translations.literal: Public and private requests submitted to them turned only on goods and money.
translations.idiomatic: Every petition, public or private, was answered only with a price tag.

sentences.zh: 舟車之利，水陸無遺；

translations.literal: The profits of boats and carts—by water and land, nothing was overlooked;
translations.idiomatic: They seized every profit to be had from boats and carts, by water and by land;

sentences.zh: 山澤之饒，所在固護；

translations.literal: the bounty of mountains and marshes—wherever found, they firmly guarded it;
translations.idiomatic: the riches of mountains and marshes wherever they could claim them;

sentences.zh: 剝削六鎮，交通互市。

translations.literal: they stripped the Six Garrisons and trafficked at the frontier markets.
translations.idiomatic: they plundered the Six Garrisons and traded at the frontier markets.

sentences.zh: 歲入利息以巨萬計。

translations.literal: Annual income in interest ran to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Their annual profits ran to millions.

sentences.zh: 又頗役嬪御，時有徵求；

translations.literal: They also frequently pressed the palace women into service and from time to time made demands;
translations.idiomatic: They also drafted palace women for labor and made constant demands upon them;

sentences.zh: 婦女器物，公然受納。

translations.literal: women's goods and utensils they openly accepted.
translations.idiomatic: women's valuables they openly accepted as bribes.

sentences.zh: 逼奪隣居，廣開室宇。

translations.literal: They forced out their neighbors and widely opened new halls and chambers.
translations.idiomatic: They seized their neighbors' land and expanded their mansions without limit.

sentences.zh: 天下咸患苦之。

translations.literal: All under Heaven alike were afflicted and grieved by them.
translations.idiomatic: The whole empire groaned under their exactions.

sentences.zh: 正光四年三月，薨于位，年六十。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year of Zhengguang, he died in office, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year of Zhengguang he died in office at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 賵帛七百匹、錢四十萬、蠟二百斤。

translations.literal: Seven hundred bolts of silk, four hundred thousand in cash, and two hundred jin of wax were sent as funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Seven hundred bolts of silk, four hundred thousand cash, and two hundred jin of wax were granted for his funeral.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚少卿護喪事。

translations.literal: The Vice Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception oversaw the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception oversaw the funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 中官為義息，衰絰者四十餘人。

translations.literal: Eunuchs as his sons by adoption in mourning dress numbered more than forty.
translations.idiomatic: More than forty eunuchs who had been his adopted sons wore mourning for him.

sentences.zh: 騰之初治宅也，奉車都尉周特為之筮，不吉，深諫止之，騰怒而不用。

translations.literal: When Teng first began building his residence, Commandant of the Imperial Carriage Zhou Te divined for it; the omen was inauspicious, and he deeply remonstrated to stop it, but Teng grew angry and did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Teng first began building his mansion, Commandant of the Imperial Carriage Zhou Te cast the divination and received an ill omen; he urgently warned him to stop, but Teng flew into a rage and ignored him.

sentences.zh: 特告人曰：「必困於三月、四月之交。

translations.literal: Te told others, "He is sure to be trapped between the third and fourth months.
translations.idiomatic: Te told others, "He is sure to meet disaster between the third and fourth months.

sentences.zh: 」至是果死，廳事甫成，陳屍其下。

translations.literal: " At this he indeed died; the reception hall had just been completed, and his corpse was laid out beneath it.
translations.idiomatic: " And so it proved: he died just as the reception hall was finished, his corpse laid out beneath its roof.

sentences.zh: 追贈使持節、驃騎大將軍、太尉公、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted bearer of the staff of authority, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Duke of Grand Minister, and Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Bearer of the Staff, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Duke of Grand Minister, and Inspector of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 騰之葬日，閹官為義服，杖絰衰縞者以百數，朝貴皆從，軒蓋填塞，相屬郊野。

translations.literal: On the day of Teng's burial, eunuchs in mourning dress for adopted sons, wearing staffs and hemp mourning bands in white, numbered in the hundreds; court nobles all followed, chariots and canopies filling and blocking the road, extending one after another across the suburbs and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of Teng's burial, hundreds of eunuchs in mourning dress for adopted sons walked with staffs and hemp bands; court nobles followed in such numbers that chariots and canopies choked the roads from the capital to the countryside.

sentences.zh: 魏初以來，權閹存亡之盛莫及焉。

translations.literal: Since the beginning of Wei, no powerful eunuch in life or death had equaled such splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of Wei, no powerful eunuch, living or dead, had ever known such splendor.

sentences.zh: 靈太后反政，追奪爵位，發其冢，散露骸骨，沒入財產。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling restored her rule, she revoked his titles posthumously, opened his tomb, scattered and exposed his bones, and confiscated his property.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling regained power, she stripped him posthumously of his titles, opened his tomb, scattered his bones, and confiscated his estate.

sentences.zh: 後騰所養一子叛入蕭衍，太后大怒，因徙騰餘養於北裔，尋遣密使追殺之於汲郡。

translations.literal: Later one of the sons Teng had raised defected to Xiao Yan; the empress dowager was greatly enraged and therefore banished Teng's remaining adopted sons to the northern frontier, then soon dispatched a secret envoy to pursue and kill them in Ji Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later one of Teng's adopted sons defected to Liang; the empress dowager was furious and exiled his remaining adopted sons to the far north, then sent secret agents to hunt them down and kill them in Ji Commandery.

sentences.zh: 賈粲，字季宣，酒泉人也。

translations.literal: Jia Can, styled Jixuan, was a man of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Can, styled Jixuan, came from Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 太和中，坐事腐刑。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, because of an offense he suffered castration.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era he was sentenced to castration for an offense.

sentences.zh: 頗涉書記。

translations.literal: He was fairly versed in writing and records.
translations.idiomatic: He had a fair acquaintance with written records.

sentences.zh: 世宗末，漸被知識，得充內侍。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Shizong's reign, he gradually came to be recognized and was able to serve as an inner attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he gradually came to notice and was admitted to inner palace service.

sentences.zh: 自崇訓丞為長兼中給事中、中嘗藥典御，轉長兼中常侍。

translations.literal: From Assistant of the Chongxun Palace Stud he became concurrently long-term Attendant Within of the Central Directorate and Director of the Internal Pharmacy, then was transferred to concurrently long-term Regular Attendant Within.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Assistant in the Chongxun Palace Stud to serve concurrently as Attendant Within in the Central Directorate and Director of the Internal Pharmacy, then as concurrent Regular Attendant Within.

sentences.zh: [13]遷光祿少卿、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: [13]He was transferred to Vice Director of Splendid Happiness and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: [13]Various editions omit the final character of Regular Attendant (侍) in the title above; the full title cannot be shortened, as Liu Teng's biography confirms in naming Jia Can Regular Attendant Within. He was promoted to Vice Director of Splendid Happiness and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 靈太后之廢，粲與元叉、劉騰等伺帝動靜。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling was deposed, Can together with Yuan Cha, Liu Teng, and others watched the emperor's movements.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling was deposed, Can joined Yuan Cha, Liu Teng, and others in watching the emperor's every move.

sentences.zh: 右衞奚康生之謀殺叉也，靈太后、肅宗同升於宣光殿，左右侍臣俱立西階下。

translations.literal: When Right Guard Xi Kangsheng plotted to kill Cha, Empress Dowager Ling and Emperor Suzong ascended together to the Hall of Xuan Radiance, and the attending ministers all stood below the western steps.
translations.idiomatic: When Right Guard Xi Kangsheng plotted to kill Cha, Empress Dowager Ling and Emperor Xiaoming ascended together to the Hall of Xuan Radiance while the attending ministers stood below the western steps.

sentences.zh: 康生既被囚執，粲紿太后曰：「侍官懷恐不安，陛下宜親安慰。

translations.literal: Once Kangsheng had been seized and bound, Can deceived the empress dowager, saying, "The attendants are fearful and uneasy; Your Majesty should go in person to reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: Once Kangsheng had been seized, Can deceived the empress dowager, saying, "The attendants are frightened and uneasy; Your Majesty should go in person to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 」太后信之，適下殿，粲便扶肅宗於東序，前御顯陽，還閉太后於宣光殿。

translations.literal: " The empress dowager believed him; just as she came down from the hall, Can took Suzong by the arm to the eastern wing, proceeded to the Palace of Xianyang, and shut the empress dowager back in the Hall of Xuan Radiance.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager believed him; as she came down from the hall, Can took Xiaoming by the arm to the eastern wing, proceeded to the Palace of Xianyang, and shut the empress dowager back in the Hall of Xuan Radiance.

sentences.zh: 粲既叉黨，威福亦震於京邑。

translations.literal: Can being a member of Cha's faction, his power and favor also shook the capital.
translations.idiomatic: As a member of Cha's faction, Can's power and favor shook the capital.

sentences.zh: 自云本出武威，魏太尉文和之後，遂移家屬焉。

translations.literal: He claimed to originate from Wuwei, a descendant of Grand Minister Wenhe of Wei, and therefore moved his family there.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed descent from Wuwei, from the line of Grand Minister Wenhe of Wei, and moved his household there.

sentences.zh: 時武威太守韋景承粲意，以其兄緒為功曹。

translations.literal: At the time the Grand Administrator of Wuwei, Wei Jing, to please Can's wishes, made his elder brother Xu Merit Officer.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Administrator of Wuwei, Wei Jing, eager to please Can, appointed Can's elder brother Xu as Merit Officer.

sentences.zh: 緒時年向七十。

translations.literal: Xu was then nearing seventy years of age.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was then nearly seventy years old.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又以緒為西平太守，比景代下，已轉武威太守。

translations.literal: Before long he also made Xu Grand Administrator of Xiping; by the time Jing returned from his posting, Xu had already been transferred to Grand Administrator of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xu was also made Grand Administrator of Xiping; by the time Jing returned from his tour of duty, Xu had already been transferred to Grand Administrator of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 靈太后反政，欲誅粲，以叉、騰黨與不一，恐驚動內外乃止。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling restored her rule, she wished to execute Can, but because Cha and Teng's partisans were not unified, fearing to alarm inner and outer court she stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling regained power, she wished to execute Can, but because Cha and Teng's followers were not of one mind she feared alarming the court and stayed her hand.

sentences.zh: 出粲為濟州刺史，未幾，遣武衞將軍刁宣馳驛殺之，資財沒於縣官。

translations.literal: Can was sent out as Inspector of Ji Province; before long Military Guard General Diao Xuan was dispatched by post relay to kill him, and his goods were confiscated to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Can was sent out as Inspector of Ji Province; before long Military Guard General Diao Xuan was dispatched posthaste to kill him, and his property was confiscated by the state.

sentences.zh: 楊範，字法僧，長樂廣宗人也。

translations.literal: Yang Fan, styled Faseng, was a man of Guangzong in Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fan, styled Faseng, came from Guangzong in Changle Commandery.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，坐宗人劫賊被誅，範宮刑，為王琚所養，恩若父子，往來出入其家。

translations.literal: In Emperor Gaozong's time, because clansmen were bandits and executed, Fan suffered palace punishment; Wang Ju raised him, their kindness like father and son, and he came and went in and out of Ju's household.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Wencheng's reign, clansmen were executed for banditry and Fan was castrated; Wang Ju raised him with the affection of a father for a son, and Fan came and went freely in Ju's household.

sentences.zh: 範為中謁者，轉黃門、中謁者僕射、中給事中、射聲校尉，加寧遠將軍，為中尹。

translations.literal: Fan served as Attendant of the Inner Gate, transferred to Yellow Gate, Vice Director of Inner Gate Attendants, Attendant Within of the Central Directorate, Commandant of the Archers' Unit, additionally made General Who Pacifies the Distance, and became Director of the Central Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Fan served as Attendant of the Inner Gate, then rose through Yellow Gate Attendant, Vice Director of Inner Gate Attendants, Attendant Within in the Central Directorate, and Commandant of the Archers' Unit, was also made General Who Pacifies the Distance, and became Director of the Central Directorate.

sentences.zh: 世宗崩，高陽王雍總政，出為白水太守，加龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong died, Prince of Gaoyang Yong took overall governance; Fan was sent out as Grand Administrator of Baishui, additionally made General of the Flying Dragon.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu died, Prince Yong of Gaoyang took overall governance and sent Fan out as Grand Administrator of Baishui with the additional rank of General of the Flying Dragon.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，徵為常侍、崇訓太僕卿，領中嘗藥典御，賜爵華陰子。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling held court, he was summoned as Regular Attendant, Grand Master of the Chongxun Palace Stud, heading the Internal Pharmacy, granted the title Viscount of Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Dowager Ling's regency he was recalled as Regular Attendant and Grand Master of the Chongxun Palace Stud, put in charge of the Internal Pharmacy, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Huayin.

sentences.zh: 為平西將軍、華州刺史。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 中官內侍貴者，[14]靈太后皆許其方岳，以範年長，拜跪為難，所司非要，故得早遂其請。

translations.literal: [14]For eminent eunuchs serving within the palace, Empress Dowager Ling granted them all provincial posts; because Fan was advanced in years and found bowing and kneeling difficult, the offices involved were not essential, and so he was able early to have his request fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: [14]Various editions omit the character for 'within'; the text is restored here per the History of the Northern Dynasties. For eminent eunuchs in inner palace service, Empress Dowager Ling granted provincial governorships to all who asked; because Fan was elderly and found court ritual arduous, and because his posts were not critical to palace affairs, his request was granted early.

sentences.zh: 父子納貨，勞役兵民，為御史所糾。

translations.literal: Father and son accepted bribes and forced soldiers and commoners into labor; they were impeached by the censor.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son accepted bribes and forced soldiers and commoners into labor; they were impeached by the censor.

sentences.zh: 子遂逃竄，範事得散。

translations.literal: The son fled and went into hiding; Fan's case was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The son fled; Fan's case was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 赴京師，遂廢於家。

translations.literal: He went to the capital and was then dismissed to remain at home.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the capital and was dismissed to remain at home.

sentences.zh: 後靈太后念範勤舊。

translations.literal: Later Empress Dowager Ling remembered Fan's long service.
translations.idiomatic: Later Empress Dowager Ling remembered Fan's long service.

sentences.zh: 乃以範為中侍中、安南將軍，尋進鎮南將軍、崇訓太僕、華州大中正。

translations.literal: She then made Fan Attendant Within, General Who Pacifies the South, soon advancing him to General Who Guards the South, Grand Master of the Chongxun Palace Stud, and Chief Arbiter of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: She restored him as Attendant Within and General Who Pacifies the South, soon promoting him to General Who Guards the South, Grand Master of the Chongxun Palace Stud, and Chief Arbiter of Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈征西將軍、秦州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted General Who Campaigns West and Inspector of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously enfeoffed as General Who Campaigns West and Inspector of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 成軌，字洪義，上谷居庸人。

translations.literal: Cheng Gui, styled Hongyi, was a man of Juyong in Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Gui, styled Hongyi, came from Juyong in Shanggu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 少以罪刑，入事宮掖，以謹厚稱。

translations.literal: While young he suffered penal punishment and entered service in the palace women's quarters; he was known for prudence and steadiness.
translations.idiomatic: Punished while still young, he entered palace service and was known for prudence and steadiness.

sentences.zh: 除中謁者僕射。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of Inner Gate Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Director of Inner Gate Attendants.

sentences.zh: 高祖意有所欲，軌瞻候容色，時有奏發，輒合帝心。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu desired something, Gui watched and awaited his expression; whenever he offered a proposal, it always matched the emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen wanted something, Gui watched his expression and, whenever he offered a suggestion, it always matched the emperor's mind.

sentences.zh: 從駕南征，專進御食。

translations.literal: Accompanying the emperor on the southern campaign, he was solely charged with presenting imperial food.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign he was solely charged with presenting the emperor's meals.

sentences.zh: 于時高祖不豫，常居禁中，晝夜無懈。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Gaozu was unwell; Gui constantly remained within the forbidden precincts, day and night without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen fell ill, Gui remained constantly within the inner palace, day and night without rest.

sentences.zh: 車駕還，賜帛百匹。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned, he was granted one hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage returned, he was granted one hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 景明中，嘗食典御丞，僕射如故。

translations.literal: In the Jingming era he served as Assistant Director of the Imperial Food Service, his vice directorship remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingming era he served as Assistant Director of the Imperial Food Service while retaining his vice directorship.

sentences.zh: 轉中給事中、步兵校尉，敕侍東宮。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Within of the Central Directorate and Commandant of the Foot Soldiers; ordered to attend the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Attendant Within in the Central Directorate and Commandant of the Foot Soldiers and ordered to attend the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 延昌末，遷中常侍、中嘗食典御、光祿大夫，賜始平伯，[15]統京染都將，轉崇訓太僕少卿。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yanchang era, he was transferred to Regular Attendant Within, Director of the Imperial Food Service, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, granted the title Baron of Shiqiping, [15] put in charge of the Capital Dye Works Commandant, and transferred to Vice Director of the Chongxun Palace Stud.
translations.idiomatic: [15]Below it says he was enfeoffed in the second year of Xiaochang as Baron of a state-founding fief of Shiqiping County; Baron (伯) here may be an error for Viscount (子) or Baronet (男), as in Wang Wen's biography, where he was first Baron of Luancheng and later Marquis of a state-founding fief. At the end of the Yanchang era he was promoted to Regular Attendant Within, Director of the Imperial Food Service, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed as Baron of Shiqiping, put in charge of the Capital Dye Works, and transferred to Vice Director of the Chongxun Palace Stud.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，詔遣主書常顯景弔慰。

translations.literal: When he suffered his mother's death, an edict dispatched Senior Clerk Chang Xianjing to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, an edict dispatched Senior Clerk Chang Xianjing to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 又起為本官，進安東將軍、崇訓衞尉卿。

translations.literal: He was recalled to his former office, advanced to General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of the Chongxun Guard.
