translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to his former office and promoted to General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of the Chongxun Guard.

sentences.zh: 久之，超遷中侍中、撫軍將軍，典御、崇訓如故。

translations.literal: After a long time he was exceptionally promoted to Attendant Within and General Who Pacifies the Army, his posts in the Food Service and Chongxun remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was exceptionally promoted to Attendant Within and General Who Pacifies the Army while retaining his posts in the Food Service and Chongxun.

sentences.zh: 尋除中軍將軍、燕州大中正。

translations.literal: Soon removed and made General of the Central Army and Chief Arbiter of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made General of the Central Army and Chief Arbiter of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 孝昌二年，以勤舊封始平縣開國伯，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaochang, for long service he was enfeoffed as Baron of a state-founding fief of Shiqiping County with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiaochang, for long service he was enfeoffed as Baron of a state-founding fief of Shiqiping County with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 肅宗所幸潘嬪，以軌為假父，頗為中官之所敬憚。

translations.literal: The concubine Pan whom Emperor Suzong favored took Gui as her nominal father; he was much respected and feared among the eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Concubine Pan, whom Emperor Xiaoming favored, took Gui as her nominal father; he was much respected and feared among the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 建義初，軌迎於河陰，詔令安慰宮內，進爵為侯，增戶三百，并前六百戶，遷衞將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi, Gui went to Heyin to meet the emperor; by edict he was ordered to reassure those within the palace, advanced in rank to marquis with three hundred additional households, six hundred in all together with what he had before, and transferred to General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyi, Gui went to Heyin to meet the emperor; by edict he was ordered to reassure those within the palace, raised to marquis with three hundred additional households for six hundred in all, and promoted to General of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 其年八月卒，贈車騎大將軍、雍州刺史，諡曰孝惠。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of that year he died; posthumously granted Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Yong Province, posthumous name Xiaohui.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month of that year and was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Yong Province, with the posthumous name Xiaohui.

sentences.zh: 養弟子仲慶，襲。

translations.literal: He raised his younger brother's son Zhongqing as his heir; Zhongqing inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He adopted his younger brother's son Zhongqing, who inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 歷位鎮軍將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of General Who Guards the Army and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General Who Guards the Army and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子朏，襲。

translations.literal: His son Fei inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fei inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, by precedent his rank was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, his rank was reduced by established rule.

sentences.zh: 王溫，字桃湯，趙郡欒城人。

translations.literal: Wang Wen, styled Taotang, was a man of Luancheng in Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wen, styled Taotang, came from Luancheng in Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父冀，高邑令，坐事被誅。

translations.literal: His father Ji was Magistrate of Gaoyi; because of an offense he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ji was Magistrate of Gaoyi and was executed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 溫與兄繼叔俱充宦者。

translations.literal: Wen and his elder brother Jishu both served as eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Wen and his elder brother Jishu both entered service as eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 高祖以其謹慎，補中謁者、小黃門，轉中黃門、鈎盾令。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu, because of his prudence, appointed him Inner Gate Attendant and Junior Yellow Gate Attendant, transferred to Central Yellow Gate Attendant and Director of the Halberd Shield.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen, because of his prudence, appointed him Inner Gate Attendant and Junior Yellow Gate Attendant, then transferred him to Central Yellow Gate Attendant and Director of the Halberd Shield.

sentences.zh: 稍遷中嘗食典御、中給事中，給事東宮，加左中郎將。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Director of the Imperial Food Service, Attendant Within of the Central Directorate, Attendant Service in the Eastern Palace, additionally made General of the Left Middle Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director of the Imperial Food Service and Attendant Within in the Central Directorate, served in the Eastern Palace, and was also made General of the Left Middle Guard.

sentences.zh: 世宗之崩，羣官迎肅宗於東宮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong died, the officials all went to welcome Emperor Suzong at the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu died, the officials went to the Eastern Palace to welcome Emperor Xiaoming.

sentences.zh: 溫於臥中起肅宗，與保母扶抱肅宗，入踐帝位。

translations.literal: Wen roused Suzong from his bed, and together with the nursemaids supported and embraced him as he ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Wen roused Xiaoming from his bed; together with the nursemaids he supported the boy as he ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 高陽王雍既居冢宰，慮中人朋黨，出為鉅鹿太守，加龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: Prince of Gaoyang Yong having become Chief Minister, fearing faction among the inner courtiers, sent Wen out as Grand Administrator of Julu, additionally made General of the Flying Dragon.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong of Gaoyang, having become Chief Minister, fearing faction among the inner courtiers, sent Wen out as Grand Administrator of Julu with the additional rank of General of the Flying Dragon.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，徵還為中常侍、光祿大夫，賜爵欒城伯，安東將軍，領崇訓太僕少卿。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling held court, he was summoned back as Regular Attendant Within, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, granted the title Baron of Luancheng, General Who Pacifies the East, heading the Vice Directorship of the Chongxun Palace Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Dowager Ling's regency he was recalled as Regular Attendant Within and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed as Baron of Luancheng, made General Who Pacifies the East, and put in charge of the Vice Directorship of the Chongxun Palace Stud.

sentences.zh: 特除使持節、散騎常侍、撫軍將軍、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: He was specially appointed Bearer of the Staff with Full Powers, Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Inspector of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially appointed Bearer of the Staff with Full Powers, Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Inspector of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 還，除中侍中，進號鎮東將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: On his return he was made Attendant Within, advanced in title to General Who Guards the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Attendant Within and promoted to General Who Guards the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal.

sentences.zh: 遷車騎將軍、左光祿大夫、光祿勳卿，侍中如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of Chariots and Cavalry, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Director of the Office of Splendid Happiness, his Attendant Within post remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General of Chariots and Cavalry, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Director of the Office of Splendid Happiness while retaining his post as Attendant Within.

sentences.zh: 孝昌二年，封欒城縣開國侯，邑六百戶。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaochang he was enfeoffed as Marquis of a state-founding fief of Luancheng County with a fief of six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiaochang he was enfeoffed as Marquis of a state-founding fief of Luancheng County with six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 溫後自陳本陽平武陽人，於是改封武陽縣開國侯，邑如故。

translations.literal: Wen later declared himself originally a man of Wuyang in Yangping, whereupon his fief was changed to Marquis of a state-founding fief of Wuyang County, the fief households remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: Wen later claimed origin from Wuyang in Yangping Commandery, and his fief was accordingly changed to Marquis of a state-founding fief of Wuyang County with the same number of households.

sentences.zh: 建義初，於河陰遇害，年六十六。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi he was killed at Heyin, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyi he was killed at Heyin, aged sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 永安初，贈驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an he was posthumously granted Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Bearer of Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yong'an he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Bearer of Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 養子冏哲，襲。

translations.literal: His adopted son Jiongzhe inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His adopted son Jiongzhe inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, by precedent his rank was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, his rank was reduced by established rule.

sentences.zh: 孟鸞，字龍兒，不知何許人。

translations.literal: Meng Luan, styled Long'er, was a man of unknown origin.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Luan, styled Long'er, came from an unknown place.

sentences.zh: 坐事充閹人。

translations.literal: Because of an offense he was made a palace eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: Punished for an offense, he entered service as a palace eunuch.

sentences.zh: 文明太后時，王遇有寵，鸞以謹敏為遇左右，往來方山，營諸寺舍。

translations.literal: In Empress Dowager Wenming's time Wang Yu was favored; Luan, for his prudence and quickness, served at Yu's side, going back and forth to Mount Fang to oversee various monasteries and halls.
translations.idiomatic: During Empress Dowager Wenming's regency Wang Yu held favor; Luan, valued for prudence and quickness, attended Yu and traveled to Mount Fang to oversee monasteries and halls.

sentences.zh: 由是漸見眷識。

translations.literal: From this he gradually came to be favored and recognized.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he gradually won favor and recognition.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，為左中郎將、中給事中。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling held court, he was made General of the Left Middle Guard and Attendant Within of the Central Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Dowager Ling's regency he was made General of the Left Middle Guard and Attendant Within in the Central Directorate.

sentences.zh: 素被病，面常黯黑，於九龍殿下暴疾，半身不攝，扶載歸家，其夜亡。

translations.literal: He had long suffered illness; his face was habitually dark. At the Hall of the Nine Dragons he was suddenly stricken—half his body lost control; he was supported and carried home, and died that night.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been ill and his face was habitually dark. At the Hall of the Nine Dragons he was suddenly stricken, half his body paralyzed; carried home in a litter, he died that night.

sentences.zh: 鸞初出，靈太后聞之，曰：「鸞必不濟，我為之憂。

translations.literal: When Luan first went out, Empress Dowager Ling heard of it and said, "Luan will surely not recover; I am anxious for him."
translations.idiomatic: When Luan first went out, Empress Dowager Ling heard of it and said, "Luan will surely not recover—I am anxious for him."

sentences.zh: 」及奏其死，為之下淚，曰：「其事我如此，不見我一日忻樂時也。

translations.literal: When his death was reported she shed tears and said, "He served me so faithfully, yet never saw me for a single day in gladness."
translations.idiomatic: When his death was reported she wept and said, "He served me so faithfully, yet never lived to see me glad even for a day."

sentences.zh: 」遂賜帛三百匹、黃絹十匹以供喪用。

translations.literal: She then granted three hundred bolts of silk and ten bolts of yellow gauze for funeral expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Various editions omit the character for gauze in yellow silk gauze; the text is restored here per the History of the Northern Dynasties. She then granted three hundred bolts of silk and ten bolts of yellow gauze for funeral expenses.

sentences.zh: [16]七日，靈太后為設二百僧齋，賜助施五十匹。

translations.literal: [16]On the seventh day Empress Dowager Ling held a vegetarian feast for two hundred monks and granted fifty bolts as aid for the rites.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day Empress Dowager Ling held a vegetarian feast for two hundred monks and granted fifty bolts of silk as aid for the rites.

sentences.zh: 同類榮焉。

translations.literal: His fellows in the eunuch caste took it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: His fellows among the eunuchs took it as an honor.

sentences.zh: 平季，字稚穆，燕國薊人。

translations.literal: Ping Ji, styled Zhimu, was a man of Ji in Yan State.
translations.idiomatic: Ping Ji, styled Zhimu, came from Ji in Yan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖濟，武威太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ji was Grand Administrator of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ji served as Grand Administrator of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 父雅，州秀才，與沙門法秀謀反，伏誅。

translations.literal: His father Ya was a provincial graduate; together with the monk Faxian he plotted rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ya, a provincial graduate, plotted rebellion with the monk Faxian and was executed.

sentences.zh: 季坐腐刑，入事宮掖。

translations.literal: Ji suffered castration and entered service in the palace women's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was castrated and entered palace service.

sentences.zh: 久之，除小黃門，以忤旨出為潞縣令，不拜。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed Junior Yellow Gate Attendant; for going against the imperial will he was sent out as Magistrate of Lu County but did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was appointed Junior Yellow Gate Attendant; for defying the throne he was sent out as Magistrate of Lu County but declined the post.

sentences.zh: 仍除奉朝請。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Attendant at Court.

sentences.zh: 靈太后反政，授寧朔將軍、長水校尉，領黃門令。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling restored her rule, he was granted General Who Pacifies the North, Commandant of the Long River, and put in charge of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling regained power he was made General Who Pacifies the North and Commandant of the Long River, with charge of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 轉前軍將軍、中給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Vanguard and Attendant Within of the Central Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General of the Vanguard and Attendant Within in the Central Directorate.

sentences.zh: 時四方多事，太后每令季出使於外。

translations.literal: At that time trouble arose on every side, and the empress dowager repeatedly sent Ji on missions abroad.
translations.idiomatic: With trouble on every side, the empress dowager repeatedly sent Ji on missions beyond the capital.

sentences.zh: 後慰勞西軍，還至潼關，華州羌人舜明等據嶮作逆，都督姜道明不能進討。

translations.literal: Later, while returning from comforting the western army and reaching Tong Pass, the Qiang of Hua Province, Shunming and others, seized the passes and rebelled; the Area Commander Jiang Daoming could not advance to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Later, returning from comforting the western army, he reached Tong Pass to find Shunming and other Qiang of Hua Province holding the passes in rebellion; Area Commander Jiang Daoming could not advance against them.

sentences.zh: 會舜明遣十餘人詐降入道明軍。

translations.literal: It happened that Shunming sent more than ten men to feign surrender and enter Daoming's army.
translations.idiomatic: Shunming then sent more than ten men to feign surrender and infiltrate Daoming's army.

translations.literal: 〈Lacuna〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Text missing in the received version.〉

sentences.zh: 遂散。

translations.literal: Thereupon they dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels thereupon dispersed.

sentences.zh: 子世冑，襲。

translations.literal: His son Shizhou inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shizhou inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, by precedent his rank was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, his rank was reduced by established rule.

sentences.zh: 封津，字醜漢，勃海蓨人也。

translations.literal: Feng Jin, styled Chouhan, was a man of Tiao in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jin, styled Chouhan, came from Tiao in Bohai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖羽，真君中為薄骨律鎮副將，以貪汙賜死。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yu, in the Zhenjun era, served as deputy general of Boguili Garrison and was granted death for corruption.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu served as deputy general of Boguili Garrison in the Zhenjun era and was sentenced to death for corruption.

sentences.zh: 父令德，娶党寶女，[18]寶伏誅，令德以連坐從法。

translations.literal: His father Lingde married the daughter of Dang Bao; [18]when Bao was executed Lingde suffered joint punishment under the law.
translations.idiomatic: [18]The History of the Northern Dynasties reads Chang rather than Dang for Bao's surname; Chang Bao is unattested elsewhere in the records and the name may be corrupt. Lingde married Bao's daughter; when Bao was executed Lingde suffered joint punishment.

sentences.zh: 津受刑，給事宮掖。

translations.literal: Jin suffered punishment and served in the palace women's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was punished and entered palace service.

sentences.zh: 積官久之，除中謁者僕射，遷奉車都尉。

translations.literal: After long accumulation of offices he was appointed Vice Director of Inner Gate Attendants and transferred to Commandant of the Imperial Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: After long service he was appointed Vice Director of Inner Gate Attendants and promoted to Commandant of the Imperial Carriages.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，冀州大乘賊起，詔津慰勞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaoming's reign the Dacheng rebels rose in Ji Province; an edict ordered Jin to offer comfort.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaoming's reign the Dacheng rebels rose in Ji Province, and an edict ordered Jin to offer comfort.

sentences.zh: 津世不居桑梓，故不為州鄉所歸。

translations.literal: Jin's family for generations had not dwelt in their native place, and so he was not accepted by the province and district.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's family had long lived away from their native place, and local people did not look to him.

sentences.zh: 靈太后令津侍肅宗書。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling ordered Jin to attend Emperor Xiaoming's correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling ordered Jin to attend Emperor Xiaoming's correspondence.

sentences.zh: 遷常山太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Administrator of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand Administrator of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，除中侍中，加征虜將軍，仍除崇訓太僕，領宮室都將，冀州大中正。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang he was made Attendant Within, additionally granted General Who Captures the Barbarians, then made Grand Master of the Chongxun Palace Stud, put in charge of the Palace Works Commandant, and Chief Arbiter of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiaochang he was made Attendant Within and General Who Captures the Barbarians, then Grand Master of the Chongxun Palace Stud, put in charge of palace construction, and Chief Arbiter of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 超拜金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was exceptionally promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal.
translations.idiomatic: He was exceptionally promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal.

sentences.zh: 二年，封東光縣開國子，食邑二百戶，鎮南將軍，兼中關右慰勞大傳。

translations.literal: In the second year he was enfeoffed as Viscount of a state-founding fief of Dongguang County with a fief of two hundred households, made General Who Guards the South, and concurrently Central Envoy to Comfort the Right of the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was enfeoffed Viscount of a state-founding fief of Dongguang County with two hundred households, made General Who Guards the South, and concurrently envoy to comfort the region west of the passes.

sentences.zh: [19]出為散騎常侍、征東將軍、濟州刺史。

translations.literal: [19]He was sent out as Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, General Who Campaigns East, and Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: [19]Various editions read Grand Tutor where envoy is meant; as in Li Daoyuan's biography, a Passes Envoy is attested in the records, and for a eunuch the title takes the prefix Central. Jin was sent out as Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, General Who Campaigns East, and Inspector of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 永安初，中侍中、衞將軍，尋轉大長秋、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an he was Attendant Within and General of the Guard; soon transferred to Grand Director of the Palace Domestic Service and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yong'an he served as Attendant Within and General of the Guard, soon transferring to Grand Director of the Palace Domestic Service and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，驃騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Bearer of Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taichang he was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Bearer of Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 津少長宮闈，給事左右，善候時情，號為機悟。

translations.literal: Jin from youth grew up within the palace women's quarters, serving at the emperor's side; skilled at reading the temper of the times, he was called quick-witted.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had grown up within the inner palace from youth, serving at the emperor's side; skilled at reading the temper of the times, he was known as quick-witted.

sentences.zh: 天平初，除開府儀同三司、本將軍、懷州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping he was made Bearer of Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies with an open office, retained his generalship, and made Inspector of Huai Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping he was made Bearer of Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies with an open office, retained his generalship, and was made Inspector of Huai Province.

sentences.zh: 元象初，復為中侍中、大長秋卿，仍開府儀同。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang he again became Attendant Within and Grand Director of the Palace Domestic Service, still holding open-office ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanxiang he again became Attendant Within and Grand Director of the Palace Domestic Service while retaining open-office ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 夏薨，年六十二。

translations.literal: In summer he died, aged sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in summer, aged sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈都督冀瀛幽安四州諸軍事、本將軍、司徒公、冀州刺史，諡曰孝惠。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Area Commander over the military affairs of Ji, Ying, You, and An provinces, his former generalship, Duke of the Ministry of Education, and Inspector of Ji Province; posthumous name Xiaohui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed Area Commander over Ji, Ying, You, and An, retaining his generalship, as Duke of the Ministry of Education and Inspector of Ji Province, with the posthumous name Xiaohui.

sentences.zh: 養兄子長業，襲爵。

translations.literal: He raised his elder brother's son Changye as his heir; Changye inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: He adopted his elder brother's son Changye, who inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, by precedent his rank was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, his rank was reduced by established rule.

sentences.zh: 津兄憑，字元寄。

translations.literal: Jin's elder brother Ping, styled Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's elder brother Ping, styled Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 當時逃竄，後會赦免。

translations.literal: At the time he fled and hid; later he met with an amnesty and was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: At the time he fled into hiding; later an amnesty pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 太和中，奉朝請，冀州趙郡王幹田曹參軍、定州彭城王勰水曹參軍、給事中、越騎校尉。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he was Attendant at Court, Staff Officer of the Agriculture Bureau under Prince Gan of Zhao in Ji Province, Staff Officer of the Water Bureau under Prince Xie of Pengcheng in Ding Province, Attendant Within, and Commandant of the Elite Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era he served as Attendant at Court, agriculture staff officer to Prince Gan of Zhao in Ji Province, water staff officer to Prince Xie of Pengcheng in Ding Province, Attendant Within, and Commandant of the Elite Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 以討大乘功，除左中郎將，遷龍驤將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: For merit in suppressing the Dacheng rebels he was made General of the Left Middle Guard and transferred to General of the Flying Dragon and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: For merit suppressing the Dacheng rebels he was made General of the Left Middle Guard, then General of the Flying Dragon and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，歷恒農、武邑二郡太守。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era he successively served as Grand Administrator of Hengnong and Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiaochang he served in turn as Grand Administrator of Hengnong and Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 尋除征虜將軍、光州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon removed and made General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians and Inspector of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians and Inspector of Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 還，為平東將軍、光祿大夫，轉鎮南將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: On his return he was made General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, transferred to General Who Guards the South and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, then General Who Guards the South and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal.

sentences.zh: 除衞將軍、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was made General of the Guard and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General of the Guard and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 初津被敕營出帝父廣平王陵。

translations.literal: Earlier Jin had been ordered by edict to construct the tomb of the Deposed Emperor's father, Prince of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jin had been ordered to construct the tomb of the Deposed Emperor's father, Prince of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，以營陵功，封津城陽縣開國子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era, for merit in building the tomb, Ping was enfeoffed as Viscount of a state-founding fief of Chengyang County with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongxi era, for merit in building the tomb, Ping was enfeoffed Viscount of a state-founding fief of Chengyang County with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 津自有封，乃啟轉於憑。

translations.literal: Jin already had a fief of his own and therefore memorialized to transfer it to Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Jin already held a fief and memorialized to transfer this one to Ping.

sentences.zh: 後除衞大將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later he was made Grand General of the Guard and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Grand General of the Guard and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 興和三年夏卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xinghe, in summer, he died, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the summer of the third year of Xinghe, aged sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 憑無他才伎，始終資歷，皆由於津。

translations.literal: Ping had no other talent or skill; his career from first to last owed entirely to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Ping had no talent of his own; his entire career owed to Jin.

sentences.zh: 津卒之後，憑亦無贈。

translations.literal: After Jin died Ping likewise received no posthumous grant.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin died Ping received no posthumous honors either.

sentences.zh: 子靈素，襲。

translations.literal: His son Lingsu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lingsu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, by precedent his rank was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, his rank was reduced by established rule.

sentences.zh: 津從兄荅，光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Jin's elder cousin of the same generation, Da, was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's elder cousin Da served as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 子宗顯，司徒掾。

translations.literal: His son Zongxian was a clerk in the Ministry of Education.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongxian served as a clerk in the Ministry of Education.

sentences.zh: 劉思逸，平原人。

translations.literal: Liu Siyi was a man of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Siyi came from Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 父直，武邑太守。

translations.literal: His father Zhi was Grand Administrator of Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhi served as Grand Administrator of Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 與元愉反於信都，伏誅。

translations.literal: Together with Yuan Yu he rebelled at Xindu and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Yuan Yu's rebellion at Xindu and was executed.

sentences.zh: 思逸少充腐刑。

translations.literal: Siyi while young suffered castration.
translations.idiomatic: Siyi was castrated while still young.

sentences.zh: 初為中小史，轉寺人。

translations.literal: At first he was a junior clerk, then transferred to palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a junior clerk, then became a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 久之，除小黃門，拜奉朝請，坐事免。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed Junior Yellow Gate Attendant and made Attendant at Court; because of an offense he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was appointed Junior Yellow Gate Attendant and Attendant at Court, then dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 後除東莞太守。

translations.literal: Later he was made Grand Administrator of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Grand Administrator of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 思逸雖身在閹寺，而性頗豪率，輕薄無行，好結朋遊。

translations.literal: Although Siyi was within the eunuch establishment, his nature was rather bold and free; he was frivolous and without propriety and loved to gather companions for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Though he served in the eunuch establishment, Siyi was bold and free by nature, frivolous and unrestrained, and fond of gathering companions.

sentences.zh: 又除左將軍、大長秋卿，遷中侍中、平東將軍。

translations.literal: He was again made General of the Left, Grand Director of the Palace Domestic Service, transferred to Attendant Within and General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made General of the Left and Grand Director of the Palace Domestic Service, then Attendant Within and General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 武定中，與元瑾等謀反，伏誅。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era he plotted rebellion together with Yuan Jin and others and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuding era he plotted rebellion with Yuan Jin and others and was executed.

sentences.zh: 又有張景嵩、毛暢者，咸以閽寺在肅宗左右，而並黠了，甚見知遇。

translations.literal: There were also Zhang Jingsong and Mao Chang, who because they served at the gate-palace at Emperor Xiaoming's side were both sharp and clever and greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Zhang Jingsong and Mao Chang, who served at the gate-palace at Emperor Xiaoming's side; both were sharp and clever and greatly favored.

sentences.zh: 俱為小黃門，每承間陳元叉之惡於肅宗。

translations.literal: Both were Junior Yellow Gate Attendants; whenever opportunity offered they reported Yuan Cha's wickedness to Emperor Xiaoming.
translations.idiomatic: Both served as Junior Yellow Gate Attendants and seized every chance to report Yuan Cha's wickedness to Emperor Xiaoming.

sentences.zh: 元叉之出，景嵩、暢頗有力焉。

translations.literal: In Yuan Cha's removal Jingsong and Chang had considerable part.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsong and Chang had considerable part in Yuan Cha's removal.

sentences.zh: 靈太后反政，未即戮叉。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling restored her rule she did not at once execute Cha.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling regained power she did not at once execute Cha.

sentences.zh: 時內外喧喧，云「叉還入知政事」。

translations.literal: At the time inner and outer court buzzed with talk that "Cha will return and again handle affairs of state."
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside the court buzzed with rumors that Cha would return to power.

sentences.zh: 暢等恐禍及己，乃啟肅宗，欲詔右衞將軍楊津密往殺叉。

translations.literal: Chang and the others feared disaster would reach them and therefore memorialized Emperor Xiaoming, wishing to edict Right Guard General Yang Jin to go secretly and kill Cha.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing disaster for themselves, Chang and the others memorialized Emperor Xiaoming, proposing an edict for Right Guard General Yang Jin to go secretly and kill Cha.

sentences.zh: 詔書已成，未及出。

translations.literal: The edict was already drafted but had not yet been issued.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was already drafted but not yet issued.

sentences.zh: 叉妻知之，告太后云：「景嵩、暢與清河王息巶欲廢太后。

translations.literal: Cha's wife learned of it and told the empress dowager, "Jingsong and Chang, together with Zhao, son of the Prince of Qinghe, wish to depose the empress dowager."
translations.idiomatic: Cha's wife learned of it and told the empress dowager, "Jingsong and Chang, together with Zhao, son of the Prince of Qinghe, wish to depose you."

sentences.zh: 」太后信之，責暢，暢出詔書草，以呈太后。

translations.literal: The empress dowager believed it and rebuked Chang; Chang produced the draft edict and presented it to the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager believed her and rebuked Chang; Chang produced the draft edict and showed it to her.

sentences.zh: 太后讀之，知無廢己狀，意為小解。

translations.literal: The empress dowager read it and knew there was no plan to depose her; her mind was somewhat relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Reading it, the empress dowager saw no plan to depose her and was somewhat reassured.

sentences.zh: 然叉妻構之不已，遂致疑惑。

translations.literal: Yet Cha's wife kept framing them without cease, and suspicion was finally aroused.
translations.idiomatic: But Cha's wife kept framing them, and suspicion finally took hold.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出暢為頓丘太守。

translations.literal: Before long Chang was sent out as Grand Administrator of Dunqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chang was sent out as Grand Administrator of Dunqiu.

sentences.zh: 後復出景嵩為魯郡太守。

translations.literal: Later Jingsong was also sent out as Grand Administrator of Lu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jingsong was also sent out as Grand Administrator of Lu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 乃密令御史掩暢，暢走免，尋捕殺之。

translations.literal: Thereupon she secretly ordered censors to seize Chang; Chang fled and escaped, but was soon captured and killed.
translations.idiomatic: She then secretly ordered censors to seize Chang; he fled but was soon captured and killed.

sentences.zh: 景嵩因入都，太后數其與暢同計之事，大致嫌責。

translations.literal: Jingsong thereupon entered the capital; the empress dowager repeatedly recounted his schemes together with Chang and on the whole resented and rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingsong next came to the capital, the empress dowager repeatedly recounted his plotting with Chang and broadly resented and censured him.

sentences.zh: 後為陽城、滎陽二郡太守。

translations.literal: Later he served as Grand Administrator of the two commanderies of Yangcheng and Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Grand Administrator of Yangcheng and Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 孝靜時，位至中侍中，坐事死。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaojing he rose to Attendant Within and was executed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaojing he rose to Attendant Within and was executed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰。

translations.literal: The historian says.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says.

translations.literal: 〈Lacuna〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Text missing in the received version.〉

sentences.zh: 校勘記

sentences.zh: 趙黑 北史卷九０目錄及傳文「黑」作「默」。

translations.literal: Zhao Hei: In Beishi juan 90 table of contents and main text, "Hei" is written "Mo."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Hei: Beishi juan 90 (table of contents and main text) reads Hei as Mo.

sentences.zh: 孟鸞 北史卷九０目錄及傳文「鸞」作「欒」。

translations.literal: Meng Luan: In Beishi juan 90 table of contents and main text, "Luan" (鸞) is written "Luan" (欒).
translations.idiomatic: Meng Luan: Beishi juan 90 (table of contents and main text) writes Luan (鸞) as Luan (欒).

sentences.zh: 自後逃戶占為細繭羅縠者非一 北史卷九０仇洛齊傳「細繭」作「紬綾」，冊府卷五０四

translations.literal: "Thereafter fugitive households registering as fine-cocoon silk gauze and thin silk were not few": Beishi juan 90 Biography of Chou Luoqi has "fine cocoon" as "chou and damask," Cefu juan 504
translations.idiomatic: "Thereafter fugitive households registering as fine-cocoon silk gauze and thin silk were not few": Beishi juan 90 (Chou Luoqi) reads xijian as chou and damask; Cefu juan 504

translations.idiomatic: , juan 667

translations.literal: , Zizhi Tongjian juan 120
translations.idiomatic: , Zizhi Tongjian juan 120

sentences.zh: 〈三七九０頁〉

translations.literal: 〈Page 3790〉

sentences.zh: 「細」都作「紬」。

translations.literal: All read "xi" (fine) as "chou" (紬).
translations.idiomatic: All read xi (fine) as chou (紬).

sentences.zh: 按本書卷一一０食貨志也作「細繭」，冊府兩條即出本書此傳和食貨志，「細」却都作「紬」，與北史合。

translations.literal: According to this, juan 110 of this book, Monograph on Food and Money, also has "fine cocoon"; the two Cefu entries derive from this biography and the Monograph on Food and Money in this book, yet both read "xi" as "chou," agreeing with Beishi.
translations.idiomatic: Juan 110 of this book (Monograph on Food and Money) also reads xijian; the two Cefu entries come from this biography and that monograph, yet both read xi as chou, matching Beishi.

sentences.zh: 「細」當是「紬」之訛。

translations.literal: "Xi" (fine) is surely a corruption of "chou" (紬).
translations.idiomatic: Xi (fine) is surely a corruption of chou (紬).

sentences.zh: 「繭」「綾」音形皆殊，「綾」字當是北史所改。

translations.literal: "Jian" (cocoon) and "ling" (damask) differ in sound and form; the character "ling" was surely altered in Beishi.
translations.idiomatic: Jian (cocoon) and ling (damask) differ in sound and form; ling was probably changed in Beishi.

sentences.zh: 遂歷右將軍中常侍 諸本並缺「歷右將軍中」五字，今據冊府卷六六五

translations.literal: "Then passed through Right General and Palace Attendant": all editions lack the five characters "li you jiang jun zhong"; now supplemented according to Cefu juan 665
translations.idiomatic: "Then passed through Right General and Palace Attendant": all editions omit the five characters li you jiang jun zhong; restored per Cefu juan 665

translations.literal: 〈Page 7959〉

sentences.zh: 補。

translations.literal: Supplemented.
translations.idiomatic: Restored.

sentences.zh: 后之惑薩菩薩也 南、北、殿、局四本及北史卷九０劇鵬傳、冊府卷六六六

translations.literal: "The empress's infatuation with Sa Pusa also": the Southern, Northern, Palace, and Bureau editions and Beishi juan 90 Biography of Ju Peng, Cefu juan 666
translations.idiomatic: "The empress's infatuation with Sa Pusa also": Southern, Northern, Palace, and Bureau editions; Beishi juan 90 (Ju Peng); Cefu juan 666

sentences.zh: 〈七九七二頁〉

translations.literal: 〈Page 7972〉

sentences.zh: 「薩」都作「薛」，百衲本、汲本作「薩」。

translations.literal: All read "Sa" as "Xue"; the Patchwork and Ji editions have "Sa."
translations.idiomatic: All read Sa as Xue; the Patchwork and Ji editions read Sa.

sentences.zh: 按「薛」是「薩」的本字，「菩薩」之「薩」本也作「薛」，似作「薛」是。

translations.literal: According to this, "Xue" is the original form of "Sa"; the "Sa" in "Bodhisattva" was originally also written "Xue"; writing "Xue" seems correct.
translations.idiomatic: Xue is the original form of Sa; the Sa in Bodhisattva was originally also written Xue, so Xue seems correct.

sentences.zh: 但卷一三幽后馮氏傳實作「高菩薩」，北史卷一三幽后傳同，則其人本姓高，「薩」「薛」都因涉下「菩薩」而訛。

translations.literal: But juan 13 Biography of Empress Feng of Youzhou actually has "Gao Pusa"; Beishi juan 13 biography of the Youzhou empress agrees; thus the man's surname was originally Gao; both "Sa" and "Xue" were corrupted through association with "Bodhisattva" below.
translations.idiomatic: But juan 13 (Empress Feng of Youzhou) and Beishi juan 13 both read Gao Pusa; the man's surname was Gao, and both Sa and Xue were corrupted through the following word Bodhisattva.

sentences.zh: 今姑從百衲本。

translations.literal: For now we follow the Patchwork edition.
translations.idiomatic: For now we follow the Patchwork edition.

sentences.zh: 是時有李豐之徒數人 諸本「李」作「季」，冊府卷六六五

translations.literal: "At this time there were several followers of Li Feng": in various editions "Li" is written "Ji," Cefu juan 665
translations.idiomatic: "At this time there were several followers of Li Feng": various editions read Li as Ji; Cefu juan 665

sentences.zh: 〈七九六０頁〉

translations.literal: 〈Page 7960〉

sentences.zh: 作「李」。

translations.literal: Has "Li."
translations.idiomatic: reads Li.

sentences.zh: 按卷五五劉芳傳見「中官李豐」，是馮太后時人，與此傳合。

translations.literal: According to juan 55 Biography of Liu Fang, "palace officer Li Feng" appears; he was a man of Empress Dowager Feng's time, matching this biography.
translations.idiomatic: Juan 55 (Liu Fang) mentions palace officer Li Feng, a man of Empress Dowager Feng's time, matching this biography.

sentences.zh: 「季」乃「李」之訛，今據改。

translations.literal: "Ji" is a corruption of "Li"; now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Ji is a corruption of Li; emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 進爵隴東公 諸本「隴」作「龍」。

translations.literal: "Advanced in rank to Duke of Longdong": in various editions "Long" (隴) is written "Dragon" (龍).
translations.idiomatic: "Advanced in rank to Duke of Longdong": various editions read Long (隴) as Dragon (龍).

sentences.zh: 按「龍東」無此郡名，下文稱養子顯明「襲爵，降為隴東公」。

translations.literal: According to this, "Dragon East" is not a commandery name; below it says the adopted son Xianming "inherited the title, reduced to Duke of Longdong."
translations.idiomatic: "Dragon East" is not a commandery name; below the adopted son Xianming inherits the title, reduced to Duke of Longdong.

sentences.zh: 即因祐由隴東公進封新平王，故降爵仍因舊封。

translations.literal: This is because You was advanced from Duke of Longdong to Prince of Xinping, so when the title was reduced it still followed the old enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: You had been advanced from Duke of Longdong to Prince of Xinping, so when the title was reduced it still followed the old enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 卷一０六下地形志下隴東郡屬涇州。

translations.literal: Juan 106b, Treatise on Administrative Geography, Part 2, records Longdong Commandery under Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Juan 106b (Treatise on Administrative Geography, Part 2) places Longdong Commandery under Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 「龍」字訛，今改正。

translations.literal: The character "dragon" is erroneous; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon (龍) is erroneous; corrected.

sentences.zh: 遷都曹加侍中祭酒尚書領中曹侍御 按祭酒以上是新遷官，尚書領中曹、侍御是原官，上文已云「尚書領中曹如故」，這裏「侍御」下當脫「如故」二字。

translations.literal: "Transferred to Director of the Capital Office, additionally made Attendant Within, Libationer, Master of Writing overseeing the Inner Bureau, and Attendant-in-Chief": according to this, from Libationer upward are newly transferred offices; Master of Writing overseeing the Inner Bureau and Attendant-in-Chief are original offices; above it already says "Master of Writing overseeing the Inner Bureau as before"; here beneath "Attendant-in-Chief" the two characters "as before" must have dropped out.
translations.idiomatic: "Transferred to Director of the Capital Office, additionally Attendant Within, Libationer, Master of Writing overseeing the Inner Bureau, and Attendant-in-Chief": Libationer and above are new appointments; Master of Writing overseeing the Inner Bureau and Attendant-in-Chief are original posts; above already reads "Master of Writing overseeing the Inner Bureau as before," so "as before" probably dropped out after Attendant-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 與雷党不蒙俱為羌中強族 百衲本、汲本「党」作「光」，南、北、殿、局四本作「党」。

translations.literal: "Together with Lei Dang, Bumeng were powerful clans among the Qiang": the Patchwork and Ji editions read "Dang" (党) as "Guang" (光); the Southern, Northern, Palace, and Bureau editions have "Dang."
translations.idiomatic: "Together with Lei Dang, Bumeng were powerful clans among the Qiang": Patchwork and Ji read Dang (党) as Guang (光); Southern, Northern, Palace, and Bureau editions read Dang.

sentences.zh: 按党是羌大姓，卷三太宗紀泰常四年六月見「羌酋党道子」。

translations.literal: According to this, Dang is a great Qiang surname; juan 3 Basic Annals of Emperor Taizong, sixth month of the fourth year of Taichang, records "Qiang chieftain Dang Daozi."
translations.idiomatic: Dang is a great Qiang surname; juan 3 (Emperor Taizong), sixth month of Taichang 4, records Qiang chieftain Dang Daozi.

sentences.zh: 元和姓纂輯本卷七党氏條云「本出西羌」。

translations.literal: The compiled Yuanhe Xing Zuan, juan 7, entry for the Dang clan says "originally from the Western Qiang."
translations.idiomatic: The compiled Yuanhe Xing Zuan, juan 7 (Dang clan), says "originally from the Western Qiang."

sentences.zh: 「党」字形近訛「光」。

translations.literal: "Dang" was corrupted to the visually similar "Guang."
translations.idiomatic: Dang was corrupted to the visually similar Guang.

sentences.zh: 今從南、北諸本。

translations.literal: Now we follow the Southern and Northern editions.
translations.idiomatic: Now we follow the Southern and Northern editions.

sentences.zh: 復奪爵 北史卷九二王遇傳作「復舊爵」。

translations.literal: "Restored the confiscated title": Beishi juan 92 Biography of Wang Yu has "restored the former title."
translations.idiomatic: "Restored the confiscated title": Beishi juan 92 (Wang Yu) reads "restored the former title."

sentences.zh: 較明白。

translations.literal: This is clearer.
translations.idiomatic: That reading is clearer.

sentences.zh: 這裏意謂復所奪之爵，但易誤解為又一次奪去爵位。

translations.literal: Here the meaning is that the title previously confiscated was restored, but it is easily misunderstood as another confiscation of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Here the sense is that a confiscated title was restored, but the wording easily suggests another demotion.

sentences.zh: 世宗封其妻王氏為□□縣君 百衲本闕字作相當於二字的墨釘，他本都作「雲陽」，冊府卷六六五

translations.literal: "Emperor Shizong enfeoffed his wife Lady Wang as □□ County Lady": the Patchwork edition marks the lacuna with ink dots equivalent to two characters; other editions all have "Yunyang"; Cefu juan 665
translations.idiomatic: "Emperor Shizong enfeoffed his wife Lady Wang as □□ County Lady": the Patchwork edition marks a two-character lacuna with ink dots; other editions read Yunyang; Cefu juan 665

sentences.zh: 〈七九六０頁〉

translations.literal: 〈Page 7960〉

sentences.zh: 「為縣君」連文不空。

translations.literal: "As County Lady" runs together without a gap.
translations.idiomatic: reads wei xianjun without a break.

sentences.zh: 按北魏郡君、縣君是加於婦人的爵位，自有封邑，與夫之封邑無關。

translations.literal: According to this, in Northern Wei commandery lady and county lady were titles conferred on women, with their own fiefs, unrelated to the husband's fief.
translations.idiomatic: In Northern Wei, commandery lady and county lady were titles for women with their own fiefs, independent of the husband's enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 下文劉騰封長樂縣公，其妻封鉅鹿郡君，初不從夫長樂之封，卷八三下外戚傳下胡國珍封安定郡公，妻皇甫氏封京兆郡君，繼妻梁氏封趙平郡君，亦不從夫安定之封，可證。

translations.literal: Below, Liu Teng was enfeoffed as Duke of Changle County; his wife was enfeoffed as Lady of Julu Commandery and did not follow her husband's Changle enfeoffment. Juan 83b Biographies of Affinal Kin, part 2: Hu Guozhen was enfeoffed as Duke of Anding Commandery; his wife the Lady Huangfu was enfeoffed as Lady of Jingzhao Commandery; his second wife the Lady Liang was enfeoffed as Lady of Zhaoping Commandery — likewise not following her husband's Anding enfeoffment. This confirms the point.
translations.idiomatic: Below, Liu Teng was Duke of Changle County while his wife was Lady of Julu Commandery, not Changle. Juan 83b (Affinal Kin): Hu Guozhen was Duke of Anding; Lady Huangfu was Lady of Jingzhao and Lady Liang Lady of Zhaoping, neither following Anding. This confirms the point.

sentences.zh: 這裏白整封雲陽男，其妻未必也封雲陽。

translations.literal: Here Bai Zheng was enfeoffed as Baron of Yunyang; his wife need not also have been enfeoffed as Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Here Bai Zheng was Baron of Yunyang; his wife need not have been enfeoffed as Yunyang too.

sentences.zh: 本闕縣名，冊府遂逕連上文。

translations.literal: The county name was originally missing; Cefu therefore ran it directly onto the text above.
translations.idiomatic: The county name was originally missing; Cefu ran the phrase directly onto the line above.

sentences.zh: 後人以為婦人必以夫之封邑為號，以意補缺，今從百衲本缺二字。

translations.literal: Later persons assumed a woman's title must take her husband's fief as its name and filled the lacuna at will; now we follow the Patchwork edition's two-character lacuna.
translations.idiomatic: Later editors assumed a woman's title must echo her husband's fief and filled the gap at will; we follow the Patchwork edition's two-character lacuna.

sentences.zh: 騰使詣行所 冊府卷六六五

translations.literal: "Teng sent an envoy to the place where the emperor was traveling": Cefu juan 665
translations.idiomatic: "Teng sent an envoy to the place where the emperor was traveling": Cefu juan 665

sentences.zh: 〈七九六一頁〉

translations.literal: 〈Page 7961〉

sentences.zh: 「行」下有「在」字。

translations.literal: Below "traveling" there is the character "at" (在).
translations.idiomatic: reads zai (at) after xing (traveling).

sentences.zh: 按此字似不宜省，然他處亦或作「行所」，非必脫文。

translations.literal: According to this, this character seems not fit to omit; yet elsewhere it is also written "traveling place" without it — not necessarily a lacuna.
translations.idiomatic: This character seems hard to omit, yet other passages also read xingsuo without it, so it is not necessarily missing text.

sentences.zh: 轉長兼中常侍 諸本「中常」下脫「侍」字。

translations.literal: "Transferred to Chief Attendant-in-Chief concurrently Palace Attendant": in various editions beneath "zhong chang" the character "shi" (attendant) is missing.
translations.idiomatic: "Transferred to Chief Attendant-in-Chief concurrently Palace Attendant": various editions omit shi under zhong chang.

sentences.zh: 按「中常侍」不得省稱「中常」，亦非他官之訛，上劉騰傳稱「中常侍賈粲」可證，今補「侍」字。

translations.literal: According to this, "Palace Attendant" cannot be abbreviated as "zhong chang"; it is not corruption of another office; above, Liu Teng's biography has "Palace Attendant Jia Can" as proof; now "shi" is supplemented.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant (zhongchangshi) cannot be shortened to zhong chang, nor is it another office corrupted; Liu Teng's biography above has Palace Attendant Jia Can as proof. Shi is restored.

sentences.zh: 中官內侍貴者 諸本脫「內」字，不可通，今據北史卷九０補。

translations.literal: "Palace officers, inner attendants who are esteemed": in various editions "inner" is missing and the text is unintelligible; now supplemented according to Beishi juan 90.
translations.idiomatic: "Palace officers, inner attendants who are esteemed": various editions omit nei (inner), making the text unintelligible; restored per Beishi juan 90.

sentences.zh: 賜始平伯 按下稱「孝昌二年，以勤舊封始平縣開國伯」，疑這裏「伯」當作「子」或「男」，否則下文「伯」當作「侯」，下王溫傳，先封欒城伯，「孝昌二年，封欒城縣開國侯」，事相類。

translations.literal: "Granted Baron of Shiping": according to what follows, "In the second year of Xiaochang, enfeoffed as Baron of a State-Founding Fief of Shiping County for longstanding service," one suspects here "baron" should be "viscount" or the lower "baron," otherwise below "baron" should be "marquis." Below, Wang Wen's biography: first enfeoffed Baron of Luancheng; "In the second year of Xiaochang, enfeoffed as Marquis of a State-Founding Fief of Luancheng County" — the cases are similar.
translations.idiomatic: "Granted Baron of Shiping": below reads "In Xiaochang 2, enfeoffed as Baron of a State-Founding Fief of Shiping County for longstanding service," so bo here should probably be zi or nan, or the later bo should be hou. Wang Wen was first Baron of Luancheng, then in Xiaochang 2 Marquis of a State-Founding Fief of Luancheng — a parallel case.

sentences.zh: 黃絹十匹以供喪用 諸本脫「絹」字，今據北史卷九０孟欒傳補。

translations.literal: "Ten bolts of yellow silk for funeral use": in various editions "silk" is missing; now supplemented according to Beishi juan 90 Biography of Meng Luan.
translations.idiomatic: "Ten bolts of yellow silk for funeral use": various editions omit juan (silk); restored per Beishi juan 90 (Meng Luan).

sentences.zh: 初季以兄叔良為襲季爵 按原文當作「初季以兄叔子良為後，襲季爵」，脫「子」「後」二字，語不可解。

translations.literal: "At first Ji made his elder brother Shuliang inherit Ji's title": according to the original the text should read "At first Ji made his elder brother Shuzi Liang his heir to inherit Ji's title"; "zi" and "heir" are missing and the language is unintelligible.
translations.idiomatic: "At first Ji made his elder brother Shuliang inherit Ji's title": the original probably read "At first Ji made his elder brother Shuzi Liang his heir to inherit Ji's title"; zi and hou (heir) are missing, making the passage unintelligible.

sentences.zh: 但無可參證，今不補。

translations.literal: But there is nothing with which to compare; for now we do not supplement.
translations.idiomatic: But there is no corroborating text; we do not restore it.

sentences.zh: 又除南本外，他本皆「叔」字起提行。

translations.literal: Moreover, apart from the Southern edition, all others begin a new line at the character "shu."
translations.idiomatic: Apart from the Southern edition, all others start a new line at shu.

sentences.zh: 南本「兄」字下空五格，北、殿、局三本「兄」字下注「闕」。

translations.literal: The Southern edition leaves five blank spaces below "elder brother"; the Northern, Palace, and Bureau editions note "lacuna" below "elder brother."
translations.idiomatic: The Southern edition leaves five blank spaces after xiong (elder brother); Northern, Palace, and Bureau editions annotate que (lacuna) there.

sentences.zh: 按弟名季，兄名叔，「叔」字本與上「兄」字相接，後人強為割裂，讀不可通，遂又於「兄」字下注「闕」字或空格，皆誤，今以「叔」字下六字逕接上文。

translations.literal: According to this, the younger brother's name was Ji, the elder brother's name Shu; the character "shu" originally adjoined "elder brother" above; later persons forcibly split them, making the reading unintelligible, then annotated "lacuna" or blank space below "elder brother" — all wrong; now the six characters below "shu" are run directly onto the text above.
translations.idiomatic: The younger brother was named Ji and the elder Shu; shu originally followed xiong above. Later editors split them, making the passage unreadable, then marked lacuna or blank space after xiong — all wrong. The six characters after shu are now run directly onto the preceding text.

sentences.zh: 娶党寶女 北史卷九０封津傳「党」作「常」。

translations.literal: "Married the daughter of Dang Bao": Beishi juan 90 Biography of Feng Jin has "Dang" as "Chang."
translations.idiomatic: "Married the daughter of Dang Bao": Beishi juan 90 (Feng Jin) reads Dang as Chang.

sentences.zh: 按卷八三上常英等傳有云「伏、寶、泰等州刺史」，連上文似是常英官，伏、寶、泰皆州名。

translations.literal: According to juan 83a Biographies of Chang Ying and others, there is "Inspector of Fu, Bao, Tai and other provinces"; read with the text above this seems to refer to Chang Ying's offices; Fu, Bao, and Tai are all province names.
translations.idiomatic: Juan 83a (Chang Ying and others) has "Inspector of Fu, Bao, Tai and other provinces"; read with the preceding text this seems to name Chang Ying's posts, with Fu, Bao, and Tai as provinces.

sentences.zh: 但魏無「伏」「寶」二州，「泰」見上文，是人名，則「伏」「寶」亦當是諸常之名，但外戚傳此傳脫訛，不知寶為常英何人。

translations.literal: But Wei had no provinces of "Fu" or "Bao"; "Tai" appears above and is a personal name; thus "Fu" and "Bao" must also be names of various Changs; but the Affinal Kin biography has corruption in this passage and it is unknown which Chang Ying relation Bao was.
translations.idiomatic: But Wei had no Fu or Bao provinces; Tai above is a personal name, so Fu and Bao must also be Chang family names. The Affinal Kin biography is corrupt here, and which Chang Bao was is unknown.

sentences.zh: 党寶未見紀載，疑北史作「常」是。

translations.literal: Dang Bao appears in no records; one suspects Beishi's "Chang" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Dang Bao appears nowhere else; Beishi's Chang is probably correct.

sentences.zh: 參卷八三上校記[九]。

translations.literal: See juan 83a, collation note [9].
translations.idiomatic: See juan 83a, collation note [9].

sentences.zh: 兼中關右慰勞大傳 諸本「大傳」作「太傅」，百衲本作「大傳」。

translations.literal: "Concurrently Chief Commissioner to Console the West within the Pass": in various editions "Grand Tutor" is written for "Grand Envoy"; the Patchwork edition has "Grand Envoy."
translations.idiomatic: "Concurrently Chief Commissioner to Console the West within the Pass": various editions read Grand Tutor (太傅) for Grand Envoy (大傳); the Patchwork edition reads Grand Envoy.

sentences.zh: 按卷八九酈道元傳，道元為「關右大使」，「大使」屢見紀載，封津是宦官，故加「中」字。

translations.literal: According to juan 89 Biography of Li Daoyuan, Daoyuan was "Grand Envoy to the West within the Pass"; "grand envoy" frequently appears in records; Feng Jin was a eunuch, hence the addition of "within."
translations.idiomatic: Juan 89 (Li Daoyuan) has Grand Envoy to the West within the Pass; dashi appears often in records. Feng Jin was a eunuch, hence the added zhong (within).

sentences.zh: 「使」字舊本訛「傳」，後人遂改為「太傅」。

translations.literal: The character "envoy" (使) was corrupted to "transmit" (傳) in the old text; later persons therefore changed it to "Grand Tutor."
translations.idiomatic: The old text corrupted shi (envoy) to chuan (transmit), and later editors changed it to Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 今姑從百衲本。

translations.literal: For now we follow the Patchwork edition.
translations.idiomatic: For now we follow the Patchwork edition.
